value.zh: 左藏南庫，
value.en: The Left Treasury Southern Store,
value.literal: The Left Treasury Southern Store,

value.en: (sealed reserve)
value.literal: (sealed reserve)

value.zh: 管御前激賞庫改。
value.en: was renamed from the Imperial Reward Store.
value.literal: was changed from managing the Imperial Reward Store.

value.zh: 以侍從官提領，又置提轄檢察官一員，編估局、打套局，
value.en: It was led by an attendant official, with an inspector-in-charge and the Appraisal Bureau and Packing Bureau,
value.literal: It was led by an attendant official, and one inspector-in-charge was also established, together with the Appraisal Bureau and the Packing Bureau,

value.zh: 〈（二局係揀選市舶香藥雜物等第，會其直以待貿易。）〉
value.en: (The two bureaus graded maritime spices and miscellaneous goods and assessed their value for trade.)
value.literal: (The two bureaus sorted maritime-trade spices, drugs, and miscellaneous goods by grade and assessed their value to await trade.)

value.zh: 寄樁庫，掌發賣香藥、匹帛，拘其直歸於左藏南庫。
value.en: The Deposited Reserve Store sold spices and silk, remitting the proceeds to the Left Treasury Southern Store.
value.literal: The Deposited Reserve Store sold spices and drugs and bolts of silk and cloth, collecting payment and returning it to the Left Treasury Southern Store.

value.zh: 置監官提領二人。
value.en: Two supervising officials were appointed to oversee it.
value.literal: Two supervising officials were established to lead it.

value.zh: 李進卿
value.en: Li Jinqing
value.literal: Li Jinqing

value.zh: 謙溥少通《左氏春秋》。
value.en: Qianpu mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals in youth.
value.literal: Qianpu in youth mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

value.zh: 從晉祖入汴，補殿直，奉使契丹。
value.en: Following the Jin founder into Bian, he became palace attendant and served as envoy to the Khitan.
value.literal: Following the Jin ancestor into Bian, he was appointed palace attendant and sent on mission to the Khitan.

value.zh: 少帝即位，改西頭供奉官，漢初，遷東頭。
value.en: When Emperor Shaodi took the throne he became western head tribute officer; early in Later Han he was transferred to eastern head.
value.literal: When Emperor Shaodi acceded, he was changed to western head tribute officer; at the beginning of Han he was transferred to eastern head.

value.zh: 周祖討三叛及守鄴都，謙溥往來宣密命，周祖愛之。
value.en: When Zhou's founding emperor campaigned against the Three Rebellions and held Ye capital, Qianpu carried secret orders back and forth and won his favor.
value.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Zhou campaigned against the Three Rebellions and guarded Ye capital, Qianpu went back and forth conveying secret orders; the Zhou founder favored him.

value.zh: 廣順初，遷供備庫副使。
value.en: Early in the Guangshun era he became deputy commissioner of the supply depot.
value.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun, he was transferred to deputy commissioner of the supply depot.

value.zh: 世宗征劉崇，遼州刺史張乙堅壁不下，遣謙溥單騎說之，乙以城降，以功改閑廄使。
value.en: Campaigning against Liu Chong, Emperor Shizong sent Qianpu alone on horseback to persuade Zhang Yi, prefect of Liao, who held the walls; Yi surrendered, and Qianpu was made commissioner of the idle stables.
value.literal: When Emperor Shizong campaigned against Liu Chong, Zhang Yi, prefect of Liao prefecture, held the walls and would not surrender; Qianpu was sent alone on horseback to persuade him, and Yi surrendered the city; for merit he was changed to commissioner of the idle stables.

value.zh: 師還，留為晉州兵馬都監。
value.en: When the army returned he was kept on as Jinzhou horse and foot supervisor.
value.literal: When the army returned, he was retained as Jinzhou horse and foot army supervisor.

value.zh: 以偏師入河東境，頻致克捷，世宗詔褒美之。
value.en: Leading a detached force into Hedong he won repeated victories, and Emperor Shizong issued an edict praising him.
value.literal: With a detached force he entered Hedong territory and repeatedly achieved victories; Emperor Shizong issued an edict praising him.

value.zh: 會隰州刺史孫義卒，時世宗親征淮南，謙溥謂節帥楊廷璋曰：「大寧，咽喉要地，不可闕守。
value.en: When Xi prefect Sun Yi died while Emperor Shizong was campaigning in Huainan, Qianpu told military governor Yang Tingzhang, "Daning is a vital choke point and must not be left undefended.
value.literal: When Sun Yi, prefect of Xi prefecture, died, at the time Emperor Shizong was personally campaigning in Huainan; Qianpu said to military governor Yang Tingzhang: "Daning is a vital throat-point and must not be left undefended.

value.zh: 且車駕出征，若俟報，則孤城陷矣。」
value.en: With the emperor on campaign, waiting for orders would mean the isolated city falls."
value.literal: Moreover, with the imperial carriage on campaign, if we wait for a report, the isolated city will fall."

value.zh: 廷璋即署謙溥權隰州事。
value.en: Tingzhang immediately put Qianpu in provisional charge of Xi prefecture.
value.literal: Tingzhang immediately appointed Qianpu to provisional charge of Xi prefecture affairs.

value.zh: 至郡，亟命浚城隍，嚴兵備，凡八日，幷人果以數千騎來寇。
value.en: On reaching the prefecture he urgently dredged the moat, strengthened defenses, and within eight days Jin forces raided with several thousand cavalry.
value.literal: Reaching the prefecture, he urgently ordered the moat and walls dredged and defenses tightened; within eight days the men of Bing indeed came to raid with several thousand cavalry.

value.zh: 時盛暑，謙溥單衣持扇，從二小吏登城，徐步按視戰具。
value.en: In peak summer heat Qianpu mounted the wall in light clothing with a fan, followed by two clerks, and slowly inspected the battle equipment.
value.literal: It was peak summer heat; Qianpu in light clothing holding a fan, followed by two junior clerks, mounted the wall and slowly walked inspecting battle equipment.

value.zh: 幷人退舍，後旬餘，大發衝車攻城。
value.en: The Jin forces withdrew; more than ten days later they returned with battering rams.
value.literal: The men of Bing withdrew; after more than ten days they launched battering rams on a large scale to attack the city.

value.zh: 謙溥募敢死士，得百餘人，短兵堅甲，銜枚夜縋出城。
value.en: Qianpu recruited more than a hundred dare-to-die soldiers with short weapons and strong armor, gagged and lowered from the wall by rope at night.
value.literal: Qianpu recruited dare-to-die soldiers, obtaining more than a hundred men with short weapons and strong armor, gagged and lowered by rope from the wall at night.

value.zh: 會廷璋兵至，合勢夾攻，掩其不及。
value.en: When Tingzhang's troops arrived they pincered the enemy and caught them unprepared.
value.literal: When Tingzhang's troops arrived, they combined forces in a pincer attack and caught them unprepared.

value.zh: 幷人大擾，悉眾遁去。
value.en: The Jin forces were thrown into disorder and fled with their entire army.
value.literal: The men of Bing were greatly thrown into disorder and fled with their entire force.

value.zh: 追北數十里，斬首千餘級，時顯德四年也。
value.en: Pursuing north for tens of li they counted more than a thousand heads; this was Xiande year four.
value.literal: Pursuing north for several tens of li, more than a thousand heads were cut off; this was in year four of Xiande.

value.zh: 明年五月，攻破孝義縣，以功領衢州刺史、監軍如故。
value.en: The following fifth month he captured Xiaoyi county and for his service held the post of Qu prefecture prefect while retaining army supervision.
value.literal: In the fifth month of the next year, he captured Xiaoyi county; for merit he held the post of prefect of Qu prefecture while retaining army supervision as before.

value.zh: 世宗北征，召赴行在。
value.en: When Emperor Shizong marched north he was summoned to the imperial camp.
value.literal: When Emperor Shizong campaigned north, he was summoned to the imperial camp.

value.zh: 恭帝即位，為澶州巡檢使，詔城莫州，數旬而就。
value.en: When Emperor Gongdi took the throne he became Danzhou patrol inspector; ordered to build Mo prefecture's walls, he finished in several weeks.
value.literal: When Emperor Gongdi acceded, he became Danzhou patrol inspector; an edict ordered the building of Mo prefecture's walls, completed within several tens of days.

value.zh: 改丹州刺史。
value.en: He was made prefect of Dan prefecture.
value.literal: He was changed to prefect of Dan prefecture.

value.zh: 張鑒，字德明，瀛州團練使藏英之孫。
value.en: Zhang Jian, whose courtesy name was Deming, was the grandson of Zang Ying, the regimental commander of Ying Prefecture.
value.literal: Zhang Jian, courtesy name Deming, was a grandson of Zang Ying, regimental commander of Ying Prefecture.

value.zh: 父裔，以蔭補供奉官。
value.en: His father Yi received appointment as a palace attendant through hereditary privilege.
value.literal: His father Yi entered service as a palace attendant through yin privilege.

value.zh: 鑒本將家，幼能嗜學，入衛州霖落山肄業，凡十餘年。
value.en: Though from a military family, Jian loved learning from childhood. He went to Linluo Mountain in Weizhou to pursue his studies, spending more than ten years there in all.
value.literal: Jian came from a military family yet loved learning from youth; he entered Linluo Mountain in Weizhou to study, for more than ten years in all.

value.zh: 太平興國三年，擢進士第，釋褐大理評事、監泰州紫墟榷務。
value.en: In the third year of the Taiping Xingguo era (978), he passed the jinshi examination. Upon entering official service he was appointed assessor of the Court of Judicial Review and superintendent of the Zixu monopoly office in Taizhou.
value.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he was elevated to jinshi rank; upon leaving office robes he became an assessor of the Court of Judicial Review and superintendent of the Zixu monopoly office in Taizhou.

value.zh: 升朝，為太子右讚善大夫、知婺州，就遷著作郎。
value.en: Once he entered court attendance, he served as Right Supporter-in-Attendance to the Heir Apparent and prefect of Wuzhou, and was then transferred in place to the post of Secretary of the Palace Library.
value.literal: Upon entering court attendance he served as Right Supporter-in-Attendance to the Heir Apparent and prefect of Wuzhou, then was transferred in place to Secretary of the Palace Library.

value.zh: 還，拜監察御史。
value.en: After returning to the capital, he was appointed investigating censor.
value.literal: Upon return he was appointed investigating censor.

value.zh: 奉詔決獄江左，頗雪冤滯。
value.en: By imperial order he adjudicated cases in the lower Yangtze region, clearing many long-standing injustices.
value.literal: By imperial order he adjudicated cases in the Jiangzuo region, clearing many long-standing injustices.

value.zh: 曆殿中侍御史。
value.en: He subsequently served as palace censor.
value.literal: He served successively as palace censor.

value.zh: 淳化中，盜起西蜀，王繼恩討平之，而御軍無政，其下恃功暴橫。
value.en: During the Chunhua era, rebels rose in western Shu. Wang Jien suppressed them, but he governed his troops poorly, and his subordinates relied on their military merit to act with violence and arrogance.
value.literal: During the Chunhua era, rebels rose in western Shu; Wang Jien suppressed them, but he governed his troops poorly and his subordinates relied on their merit to act with violence and arrogance.

value.zh: 益州張詠密奏，請命近臣分屯師旅，即遣鑒與西京作坊使馮守規偕往。
value.en: Zhang Yong of Yizhou secretly memorialized, requesting that close ministers be sent to station troops in separate camps. Jian was immediately dispatched together with Feng Shougui, commissioner of the Western Capital Workshop Office.
value.literal: Zhang Yong of Yizhou secretly memorialized, requesting that close ministers be sent to station troops in separate camps; Jian was immediately dispatched together with Feng Shougui, commissioner of the Western Capital Workshop Office.

value.zh: 召對後苑門，面授方略。
value.en: He was summoned for audience at the Rear Garden Gate and personally instructed in strategy.
value.literal: He was summoned for audience at the Rear Garden Gate and personally instructed in strategy.

value.zh: 鑒曰：“益部新復，軍旅不和，若聞使命驟至，易其戎伍，慮或猜懼，變生不測。
value.en: Jian said, "The Yi region has only recently been recovered, and the army is ill at ease. If the troops hear that envoys have suddenly arrived to reorganize their units, they may grow suspicious and fearful, and unforeseen trouble may arise.
value.literal: Jian said: "The Yi region has only recently been recovered and the army is ill at ease. If they hear that envoys have suddenly arrived to change their military units, they may grow suspicious and fearful, and unforeseen trouble may arise.

value.zh: 請假臣安撫之名。”
value.en: I ask that I be granted the title of pacification commissioner."
value.literal: I ask that I be granted the title of pacification commissioner."

value.zh: 太宗稱善。
value.en: Emperor Taizong praised the proposal.
value.literal: Taizong praised the proposal.

value.zh: 鑒至蜀，繼恩猶偃蹇，不意朝廷聞其縱肆。
value.en: When Jian reached Shu, Wang Jien remained insolent and did not expect the court to have heard of his excesses.
value.literal: When Jian reached Shu, Jien was still insolent and did not expect the court to have heard of his excesses.

value.zh: 鑒之行，付以空名宣頭及廷臣數人，鑒與詠即遣部戍卒出境，繼恩麾下使臣亦多遣東還，督繼恩輩分路討捕殘寇，而鑒等招輯反側。
value.en: Before Jian's departure he was given blank commission documents and several court officials. Jian and Yong immediately sent garrison troops out of the province, sent many of Wang Jien's staff envoys back east, and supervised Jien and his men in pursuing remnant bandits by separate routes, while Jian and the others won over those who were wavering.
value.literal: Before Jian's departure he was given blank commission documents and several court officials; Jian and Yong immediately sent garrison troops out of the province, also sent many of Jien's staff envoys back east, supervised Jien and his men in pursuing remnant bandits by separate routes, and Jian and the others won over the wavering.

value.zh: 事平歸朝，未至，拜左諫議大夫、戶部使。
value.en: When the affair was settled and he was returning to court, he was appointed Left Remonstrance Councillor and commissioner of the Household Bureau before he even arrived.
value.literal: When the affair was settled and he returned to court, before he arrived he was appointed Left Remonstrance Councillor and commissioner of the Household Bureau.

value.zh: 初，鑒在南海，李夷庚為通判，謝德權為巡檢，皆與之不協。
value.en: Earlier, when Jian was in the South Sea region, Li Yigeng served as vice prefect and Xie Dequan as inspector; both were at odds with him.
value.literal: Earlier, when Jian was in the South Sea region, Li Yigeng served as vice prefect and Xie Dequan as inspector; both were at odds with him.

value.zh: 二人密言鑒以貲付海賈，往來貿市，故徙小郡。
value.en: The two secretly reported that Jian had entrusted capital to maritime traders for commerce back and forth, and for this reason was transferred to a smaller prefecture.
value.literal: The two secretly reported that Jian had entrusted capital to maritime traders for commerce back and forth, and for this reason was transferred to a smaller prefecture.

value.zh: 至是，鑒自陳有親故謫瓊州，每以奉米附商舶寄贍之，又言夷庚、德權憸人貪凶之狀，上意稍釋。
value.en: At this time Jian explained himself, saying he had relatives and friends exiled to Qiongzhou whom he regularly supplied with stipend grain sent by merchant ships. He also reported the treacherous and greedy conduct of Yigeng and Dequan, and the emperor's suspicions were somewhat eased.
value.literal: At this time Jian explained himself, saying he had relatives and friends exiled to Qiongzhou whom he regularly supplied with stipend grain sent by merchant ships; he also reported the treacherous and greedy conduct of Yigeng and Dequan, and the emperor's mind was somewhat eased.

value.zh: 召還，以疾徙知相州。
value.en: Recalled to court, he was transferred to Xiangzhou on account of illness.
value.literal: Recalled to court, he was transferred to Xiangzhou on account of illness.

value.zh: 有芝草生於監牧之室，鑒表其祥異，以為河朔弭兵款附之兆。
value.en: An auspicious fungus grew in the room of the pasture office. Jian memorialized the marvel, taking it as a sign that the north would lay down arms and submit.
value.literal: An auspicious fungus grew in the room of the pasture office; Jian memorialized the marvel, taking it as a sign that the north would lay down arms and submit.

value.zh: 優詔答之。
value.en: A gracious edict replied to him.
value.literal: A gracious edict replied to him.

value.zh: 景德初，卒，年五十八。
value.en: At the beginning of the Jingde era he died, aged fifty-eight.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Jingde era he died, aged fifty-eight.

value.zh: 〇陳靖張綸邵曄崔立魯有開張逸吳遵路趙尚寬高賦程師孟韓晉卿葉康直
value.en: Chen Jing, Zhang Lun, Shao Ye, Cui Li, Lu Youkai, Zhang Yi, Wu Zunlu, Zhao Shangkuan, Gao Fu, Cheng Shimeng, Han Jinqing, and Ye Kangzhi.
value.literal: Chen Jing, Zhang Lun, Shao Ye, Cui Li, Lu Youkai, Zhang Yi, Wu Zunlu, Zhao Shangkuan, Gao Fu, Cheng Shimeng, Han Jinqing, Ye Kangzhi.

value.zh: 張逸，字大隱，鄭州滎陽人。
value.en: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Dayin, came from Xingyang in Zhengzhou.
value.literal: Zhang Yi, styled Dayin, was a native of Xingyang in Zhengzhou.

value.zh: 進士及第，為試秘書省校書郎。
value.en: Having passed the jinshi examination, he became a probationary collator in the Secretariat.
value.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was made a probationary collator in the Secretariat.

value.zh: 知襄州鄧城縣，有能名。
value.en: As magistrate of Dengcheng in Xiangzhou he earned a name for competence.
value.literal: As magistrate of Dengcheng County in Xiangzhou he gained a reputation for ability.

value.zh: 積州謝泌將薦逸，先設几案，置章其上，望闕再拜曰：「老臣為朝廷得一良吏。」
value.en: Xie Bi, the prefect, was about to recommend Yi; he set out a desk, laid the memorial on it, bowed twice toward the palace, and said, "Your old servant has secured a fine official for the dynasty."
value.literal: Prefect Xie Bi was about to recommend Yi; he first set out a desk, placed the memorial upon it, bowed twice toward the palace, and said: "This old servant has found the court a worthy official."

value.zh: 乃奏之。
value.en: Then he sent in the memorial.
value.literal: Then he submitted it.

value.zh: 他日引對，真宗問所欲何官，逸對曰：「母老在家，願得近鄉一幕職官，歸奉甘旨足矣。」
value.en: On a later audience day Emperor Zhenzong asked what post he wanted; Yi answered, "My mother is old and at home; I ask only for a county staff appointment near my native place so I can go back and support her—that is all I want."
value.literal: On another day he was summoned for audience; Zhenzong asked what office he desired; Yi replied: "My mother is old at home; I wish only a local staff post near my home county so I may return and provide for her—that is enough."

value.zh: 授澶州觀察推官，數日，以母喪去。
value.en: He was given the post of investigating officer on the Chanzong observation commission; within days he resigned to mourn his mother.
value.literal: He was appointed investigating officer on the Chanzong observation commission; within days he left office on his mother's death.

value.zh: 服除，引對，帝又固問之，對曰：「願得京官。」
value.en: When the mourning period ended he was called in again; the emperor pressed him once more, and he replied, "I would like a capital appointment."
value.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned again; the emperor pressed the question once more, and he replied: "I wish to receive a capital appointment."

value.zh: 特改大理寺丞。
value.en: He was specially appointed assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review.
value.literal: He was specially made Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

value.zh: 帝雅賢泌，再召問逸者，用泌薦也。
value.en: The emperor had always held Bi in high regard and questioned Yi again on Bi's recommendation.
value.literal: The emperor had long esteemed Bi and summoned Yi again to question him because of Bi's recommendation.

value.zh: 知長水縣，時王嗣宗留守西京，厚遇之，及徙青神縣，貧不自給，嗣宗假奉半年使辦裝。
value.en: While magistrate of Changshui, he enjoyed the warm patronage of Wang Sizong, regent of the Western Capital; when he was moved to Qingshen he could barely support himself, and Sizong advanced him half a year's salary for travel expenses.
value.literal: As magistrate of Changshui County, Wang Sizong was then regent at the Western Capital and treated him generously; when Yi was transferred to Qingshen County he was too poor to support himself, and Sizong lent him half a year's salary to prepare for the move.

value.zh: 既至縣，興學校，教生徒。
value.en: On reaching the county he founded schools and taught students.
value.literal: Once he reached the county he established schools and instructed students.

value.zh: 後邑人陳希亮、楊異相繼登科，逸改其居曰桂枝裏。
value.en: Later two local men, Chen Xiliang and Yang Yi, passed the examinations in turn, and Yi renamed his home Gui Branch Lane.
value.literal: Later townspeople Chen Xiliang and Yang Yi passed the examinations in succession, and Yi renamed his residence Gui Branch Lane.

value.zh: 縣東南有松柏灘，夏秋暴漲多覆舟，逸禱江神，不逾月，灘為徙五里，時人異之。
value.en: Southeast of the county lay Songbai Shoal, where summer and autumn floods often sank boats; Yi prayed to the river god, and within a month the shoal had shifted five li—a wonder to all who heard of it.
value.literal: Southeast of the county was Songbai Shoal; in summer and autumn sudden floods often capsized boats; Yi prayed to the river god, and in less than a month the shoal shifted five li—people of the time marveled at it.

value.zh: 再遷太常博士、知尉氏縣。
value.en: He was promoted again to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and appointed magistrate of Weishi County.
value.literal: He was again promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and made magistrate of Weishi County.

value.zh: 擢監察御史，提點益州路刑獄，開封府判官。
value.en: He was raised to investigating censor, intendant of criminal cases on the Yizhou circuit, and judge in the Kaifeng prefectural office.
value.literal: He was elevated to Investigating Censor, Intendant of Criminal Cases on the Yizhou Circuit, and judge of the Kaifeng Prefecture office.

value.zh: 使契丹，為兩浙轉運使。
value.en: He went on embassy to the Khitan and later became transport commissioner of the Two Zhes.
value.literal: He served as envoy to the Khitan and became Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhes.

value.zh: 徙陜西，未赴，又徙河東，居數月，復徙陜西。
value.en: He was posted to Shaanxi, reassigned to Hedong before he could take up the post, and after a few months sent back to Shaanxi.
value.literal: He was transferred to Shaanxi; before he took up the post he was transferred again to Hedong; after several months he was transferred back to Shaanxi.

value.zh: 以龍圖閣待制知梓州。
value.en: With the title drafting attendant at the Hall of Dragon Illustrations he became prefect of Zizhou.
value.literal: As Drafting Attendant at the Hall of Dragon Illustrations he was made prefect of Zizhou.

value.zh: 累遷尚書兵部郎中，知開封府。
value.en: He was promoted step by step to director in the Ministry of War and appointed prefect of Kaifeng.
value.literal: He rose in stages to Director in the Ministry of War in the Ministry of Revenue and was made prefect of Kaifeng.

value.zh: 有僧求內降免田稅，而逸固執不許。
value.en: A monk petitioned for an imperial exemption from land tax, but Yi steadfastly refused.
value.literal: A monk sought an internal edict exempting him from field tax, but Yi firmly refused.

value.zh: 仁宗曰：「有司能守法，朕何憂也。」
value.en: Emperor Renzong said, "When the bureaucracy keeps the law, what need have I to worry?"
value.literal: Emperor Renzong said: "When officials can uphold the law, what have I to worry about?"

value.zh: 又言：「頃禁命婦幹禁中恩，比來稍通女謁，願令官司糾劾。」
value.en: He also said, "Consorts of officials were recently barred from seeking favors inside the palace, yet lately such petitions have crept back in; I ask that the offices investigate and prosecute them."
value.literal: He also said: "Recently consorts of officials were forbidden to solicit favors within the palace; of late women have again been gaining access through petitions—I ask that the offices investigate and punish this."

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: The emperor agreed.
value.literal: The request was granted.

value.zh: 以樞密直學士知益州。
value.en: As direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs he became prefect of Yizhou.
value.literal: As Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs he was made prefect of Yizhou.

value.zh: 逸凡四至蜀，諳其民風。
value.en: Yi had been to Shu four times in all and knew its people and customs intimately.
value.literal: Yi had gone to Shu four times in all and knew its customs well.

value.zh: 華陽騶長殺人，誣道旁行者，縣吏受財，獄既具，乃使殺人者守囚。
value.en: A stable chief in Huayang killed a man and framed a traveler on the road; county clerks took bribes, and when the case was closed they put the actual killer in charge of guarding the prisoner.
value.literal: A Huayang stable chief murdered someone and framed a passerby on the road; county clerks took bribes; when the case was complete they even made the murderer guard the prisoner.

value.zh: 逸曰：「囚色冤，守者氣不直，豈守者殺人乎？」
value.en: Yi said, "The prisoner looks aggrieved, and the guard's manner is guilty—could the guard be the murderer?"
value.literal: Yi said: "The prisoner looks wronged, and the guard's bearing is not upright—could the guard be the killer?"

value.zh: 囚始敢言，而守者果服，立誅之，蜀人以為神。
value.en: Only then did the prisoner dare speak out; the guard confessed, was executed at once, and the people of Shu thought Yi almost supernatural.
value.literal: Only then did the prisoner dare speak; the guard indeed confessed, was immediately executed, and the people of Shu regarded Yi as divine.

value.zh: 會歲旱，逸使作堰壅江水，溉民田，自出公租減價以振民。
value.en: That year brought drought; Yi had a weir built to hold back river water and irrigate farmland, and from his own official income he sold grain at reduced prices to relieve the people.
value.literal: When drought struck that year, Yi had a weir built to dam the river and irrigate the people's fields, and from his own official rent he cut prices to relieve the people.

value.zh: 初，民饑多殺耕牛食之，犯者皆配關中。
value.en: Earlier, in famine years many peasants had killed draft oxen for food, and offenders were all banished to Guanzhong.
value.literal: Earlier, when the people were hungry many slaughtered plow oxen for food; offenders were all exiled to Guanzhong.

value.zh: 逸奏：「民殺牛以活將死之命，與盜殺者異，若不禁之，又將廢穡事。
value.en: Yi memorialized, "Peasants who slaughter oxen to stave off starvation are not the same as thieves who steal and kill cattle; yet if the practice is unchecked, agriculture will collapse.
value.literal: Yi memorialized: "When people kill oxen to save lives on the verge of death, it differs from killing oxen by theft; if it is not forbidden, farming will again be ruined.

value.zh: 今歲少稔，請一切放還，復其業。」
value.en: This year the harvest is fair; I ask that all such exiles be pardoned and sent home to resume farming."
value.literal: This year the harvest is somewhat good; I ask that all such offenders be released and restored to their occupations."

value.zh: 報可。
value.en: The request was approved.
value.literal: Approval was granted.

value.zh: 未幾，卒於官。
value.en: Not long afterward he died in office.
value.literal: Before long he died in office.

value.zh: 列傳第十九 殷淳子孚弟沖淡張暢何偃江智淵
value.en: Biography 19: Yin Chun, Yin Fu, Yin Chong, Yin Dan, Zhang Chang, He Yan, and Jiang Zhiyuan
value.literal: Biography 19: Yin Chun, his son Fu, younger brothers Chong and Dan, Zhang Chang, He Yan, Jiang Zhiyuan

value.zh: 張暢，字少微，吳郡吳人，吳興太守邵兄子也。
value.en: Zhang Chang, styled Shaowei, was a native of Wu in Wu Commandery and the nephew of Shao, governor of Wuxing, on his father's side.
value.literal: Zhang Chang, style Shaowei, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery, nephew of Wuxing Governor Shao by his elder brother.

value.zh: 父禕，少有孝行，歷宦州府，為琅邪王國郎中令。
value.en: His father Zhang Yi was known for filial devotion from youth and served in regional government until he was appointed chief of gentlemen in the principality of Langye.
value.literal: His father Yi in youth had filial conduct; he passed through offices in prefectures and provinces and served as Administrator of Gentlemen in the Kingdom of Langye.

value.zh: 從琅邪王至洛。
value.en: He accompanied the Prince of Langye to Luoyang.
value.literal: He followed the Prince of Langye to Luoyang.

value.zh: 還京都，高祖封藥酒一甖付褘，使密加酖毒。
value.en: On the return journey to the capital, Emperor Gaozu gave Yi a sealed jar of medicinal wine with orders to lace it secretly with lethal poison.
value.literal: Returning to the capital, Emperor Gaozu sealed a jar of medicinal wine and entrusted it to Yi, ordering him secretly to add poison.

value.zh: 褘受命，既還，於道自飲而卒。
value.en: Yi accepted the charge, and on the way home he drank the wine himself and died.
value.literal: Yi received the command; once returned, on the road he drank it himself and died.

value.zh: 肅宗孝明皇帝，諱詡，世宗宣武皇帝之第二子，母曰胡充華。
value.en: Suzong, Emperor Xiaoming, bore the taboo name Xu. He was Shizong, Emperor Xuanwu's second son; his mother was Hu Chuhua.
value.literal: Suzong, Emperor Xiaoming, bore the taboo name Xu; he was Shizong, Emperor Xuanwu's second son; his mother was Hu Chuhua.

value.zh: 永平三年三月丙戌，帝生于宣光殿之東北，有光照于庭中。
value.en: In the third year of Yongping, in the third month, on the bingxu day, the emperor was born northeast of the Xuanguang Hall; light shone in the courtyard.
value.literal: In the third year of Yongping, third month, day bingxu, the Emperor was born northeast of the Xuanguang Hall; light shone in the courtyard.

value.zh: 延昌元年十月乙亥，立為皇太子。
value.en: In the tenth month of the first year of Yanchang, on the yihai day, he was installed as crown prince.
value.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yanchang, day yihai, he was installed as crown prince.

value.zh: 二年春正月丁亥，詔曰：「朕以沖眇，纂承寶位，夙夜惟寅，若涉淵海。
value.en: In the first month of spring in the second year, on the dinghai day, an edict said, "We, young and slight, have succeeded to the precious throne; morning and evening we are reverent, as if crossing a deep sea.
value.literal: First month of spring in the second year, day dinghai: an edict said, "We, young and slight, have succeeded to the precious throne; morning and evening we are reverent, as if crossing a deep sea.

value.zh: 賴皇太后慈仁，被以夙訓。
value.en: We rely on the empress dowager's compassionate benevolence, covered with early instruction.
value.literal: We rely on the empress dowager's compassionate benevolence, covered with early instruction.

value.zh: 自臨朝踐極，歲將半紀，天平地成，四海寧乂。
value.en: Since holding court and treading the pinnacle, nearly half a reign has passed; heaven is level and earth at peace; within the four seas there is quiet.
value.literal: Since holding court and treading the pinnacle, nearly half a reign has passed; heaven is level and earth at peace; within the four seas there is quiet.

value.zh: 天道高遠，巍巍難名，猶以撝挹自居，稱號弗備，非所以崇奉坤元，允協億兆者也。
value.en: The Way of Heaven is high and far, lofty and hard to name; yet we still restrain ourselves and hold back, our title not complete—not what is meant by honoring and serving Earth's origin and harmonizing with the hundred millions.
value.literal: The Way of Heaven is high and far, lofty and hard to name; yet we still restrain ourselves and hold back, our title not complete—not what is meant by honoring and serving Earth's origin and harmonizing with the hundred millions.

value.zh: 宜遵舊典，稱詔宇內，以副黎蒸元元之望。」
value.en: We should follow the old canon and proclaim our title throughout the realm, to answer the hope of the black-haired masses."
value.literal: We should follow the old canon and proclaim our title throughout the realm, to answer the hope of the black-haired masses."

value.zh: 是月，改葬文昭皇太后高氏。
value.en: That month Empress Wenzhao of the Gao clan was reburied.
value.literal: That month Empress Wenzhao of the Gao clan was reburied.

value.zh: 二月乙丑，齊郡王祐薨。
value.en: In the second month, on the yichou day, You, Prince of Qi commandery, died.
value.literal: Second month, day yichou: Prince of Qi Commandery You died.

value.zh: 庚午，羽林千餘人焚征西將軍張彝第，毆傷彝，燒殺其子始均。
value.en: On the gengwu day more than a thousand guardsmen burned the residence of Zhang Yi, general who campaigns west, beat Yi, and burned and killed his son Shi Jun.
value.literal: Day gengwu: more than a thousand guardsmen burned the residence of General Who Campaigns West Zhang Yi, beat Yi, and burned and killed his son Shi Jun.

value.zh: 吐谷渾、宕昌國並遣使朝貢。
value.en: Tuyuhun and Dangchang both sent envoys with tribute.
value.literal: Tuyuhun and Dangchang both sent envoys with tribute.

value.zh: 乙亥，大赦天下。
value.en: On the yihai day a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
value.literal: Day yihai: a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

value.zh: 丁丑，詔求直言，諸有上書者聽密封通奏。
value.en: On the dingchou day an edict sought forthright speech; those who submitted memorials were permitted to seal them and have them forwarded.
value.literal: Day dingchou: an edict sought forthright speech; those who submitted memorials were permitted to seal them and have them forwarded.

value.zh: 壬寅，詔曰：「農要之月，時澤弗應，嘉穀未納，三麥枯悴。
value.en: On the renyin day an edict said, "In the crucial month of farming the seasonal rains have not responded; the good grain is not yet gathered; the three wheats wither.
value.literal: Day renyin: an edict said, "In the crucial month of farming the seasonal rains have not responded; the good grain is not yet gathered; the three wheats wither.

value.zh: 德之無感，歎懼兼懷。
value.en: That virtue has no effect fills us with sighs and fear together.
value.literal: That virtue has no effect fills us with sighs and fear together.

value.zh: 可敕內外，依舊雩祈，率從祀典。
value.en: Let inner and outer offices follow the old rain-prayer and lead the sacrificial canon.
value.literal: Let inner and outer offices follow the old rain-prayer and lead the sacrificial canon.

value.zh: 察獄理冤，掩胔埋骼。
value.en: Examine prisons and right wrongs; cover exposed corpses and bury bones.
value.literal: Examine prisons and right wrongs; cover exposed corpses and bury bones.

value.zh: 冀瀛之境，往經寇暴，死者既多，白骨橫道，可遣專令收葬。
value.en: In the Ji and Ying regions, which formerly suffered raids, the dead were many and white bones lay across the roads—special commissioners may be sent to gather and bury them.
value.literal: In the Ji and Ying regions, which formerly suffered raids, the dead were many and white bones lay across the roads—special commissioners may be sent to gather and bury them.

value.zh: 賑窮恤寡，救疾存老，準訪前式，務令周備。」
value.en: Relieve the poor and comfort the widowed; heal the sick and preserve the aged; consult former models and see that all is thoroughly done."
value.literal: Relieve the poor and comfort the widowed; heal the sick and preserve the aged; consult former models and see that all is thoroughly done."

value.zh: 三月甲辰，澍雨大洽。
value.en: In the third month, on the jiachen day, soaking rain fell abundantly.
value.literal: Third month, day jiachen: soaking rain fell abundantly.

value.zh: 奚斤 叔孫建
value.en: Xi Jin; Shusun Jian
value.literal: Xi Jin; Shusun Jian

value.zh: 劉義符前東牟太守清河張幸先匿孤山 張森楷云；
value.en: "Former Administrator of Dongmou under Liu Yifu, Zhang Xing of Qinghe, had earlier hidden on Gushan": Zhang Senkai says:
value.literal: "Former Administrator of Dongmou under Liu Yifu, Zhang Xing of Qinghe, had earlier hidden on Gushan": Zhang Senkai says:

value.zh: 「張彝傳
value.en: "Biography of Zhang Yi
value.literal: "Biography of Zhang Yi

value.zh: 〈卷六四〉
value.en: 〈juan 64〉
value.literal: 〈juan 64〉

value.zh: 及南燕錄並云幸是慕容超東牟太守，不聞仕宋。
value.en: and the Southern Yan records all say Xing was Murong Chao's administrator of Dongmou, with no mention of service under Song.
value.literal: and the records of Southern Yan all say Xing was Administrator of Dongmou under Murong Chao and are not heard to have served Song.

value.zh: 此『劉義符』三字恐誤。」
value.en: The three characters Liu Yifu are likely in error."
value.literal: These three characters 'Liu Yifu' are likely in error."

value.zh: 郭祚 張彝
value.en: Guo Zuo; Zhang Yi
value.literal: Guo Zuo; Zhang Yi

value.zh: 景尚弟慶禮，字叔，為祚所愛。
value.en: Jing Shang's younger brother Qingli, courtesy name Shu, was a favorite of Zuo's.
value.literal: Jing Shang's younger brother Qingli, courtesy name Shu, was beloved by Zuo.

value.zh: 著作佐郎、通直郎。
value.en: He served as Assistant Gentleman of Composition and Direct Attendant.
value.literal: [He served as] Assistant Gentleman of Composition and Direct Attendant.

value.zh: 卒，贈征虜將軍、瀛州刺史。
value.en: When he died he was posthumously granted the title General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Ying Province.
value.literal: Upon his death, he was posthumously granted the title General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Ying Province.

value.zh: 張彝，字慶賓，清河東武城人。
value.en: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Qingbin, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
value.literal: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Qingbin, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

value.zh: 曾祖幸，慕容超東牟太守，後率戶歸國。
value.en: His great-grandfather Xing had been Administrator of Dongmu under Murong Chao; later he led his household in submission to the Wei.
value.literal: His great-grandfather Xing was Administrator of Dongmu under Murong Chao; afterward he led his household to surrender to [Northern Wei].

value.zh: 世祖嘉之，賜爵平陸侯，拜平遠將軍、青州刺史。
value.en: Emperor Shizu praised him, granted him the title Marquis of Pinglu, and appointed him General of Pacifying the Distance and Governor of Qing Province.
value.literal: Emperor Shizu commended him, bestowed the title Marquis of Pinglu, and appointed him General of Pacifying the Distance and Governor of Qing Province.

value.zh: 祖準之襲，又為東青州刺史。
value.en: His grandfather Zhun inherited the title and also served as Governor of Eastern Qing Province.
value.literal: His grandfather Zhun inherited [the title] and also served as Governor of Eastern Qing Province.

value.zh: 父靈真，早卒。
value.en: His father Lingzhen died young.
value.literal: His father Lingzhen died early.

value.zh: 彝性公強，有風氣，歷覽經史。
value.en: Yi was by nature upright and forceful, possessed of moral bearing, and had read widely in the classics and histories.
value.literal: Yi was by nature forthright and forceful, possessed moral stature, and read widely in the classics and histories.

value.zh: 高祖初，襲祖侯爵，與盧淵、李安民等結為親友，往來朝會，常相追隨。
value.en: In the early years of Emperor Wen, he inherited his grandfather's marquisate and became close friends with Lu Yuan, Li Anmin, and others; at court they were often together.
value.literal: In the early years of Emperor Gaozu, he inherited his grandfather's marquisate and formed friendships with Lu Yuan, Li Anmin, and others; at court gatherings they were often in each other's company.

value.zh: 淵為主客令，安民與彝並為散令。
value.en: Lu Yuan was Director of Guests; Li Anmin and Zhang Yi were both Directors of the Scattered Cavalry.
value.literal: Yuan was Director of Guests; Anmin and Yi were both Directors of the Scattered Cavalry.

value.zh: 彝少而豪放，出入殿庭，步眄高上，無所顧忌。
value.en: From youth Zhang Yi was bold and free-spirited; entering and leaving the palace halls, he walked with his eyes lifted high, heedless of restraint.
value.literal: Yi from youth was bold and unrestrained; entering and leaving the palace hall, he walked with his gaze lifted high, without any restraint.

value.zh: 文明太后雅尚恭謹，因會次見其如此，遂召集百僚督責之，令其修悔，而猶無悛改。
value.en: Empress Dowager Wenming prized reverence and restraint. Once at court she saw him behave so and summoned the hundred officials to rebuke him publicly, ordering him to repent—but he still would not change.
value.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming greatly valued reverence and prudence; on one occasion at court she saw him behave thus, whereupon she assembled the hundred officials to supervise and rebuke him, ordering him to repent and reform—yet he still showed no change of heart.

value.zh: 善於督察，每東西馳使有所巡檢，彝恒充其選，清慎嚴猛，所至人皆畏伏，儔類亦以此高之。
value.en: He was skilled at inspection. Whenever envoys were sent east or west on tour, Yi was always chosen. Clear, cautious, strict, and stern, he inspired fear wherever he went, and his peers respected him for it.
value.literal: He was skilled at supervision and inspection; whenever emissaries were dispatched east and west for inspections, Yi was invariably chosen; clear, cautious, strict, and severe—wherever he went people feared and submitted, and his peers also held him in high regard for this.

value.zh: 遷主客令，例降侯為伯，轉太中大夫，仍行主客曹事。
value.en: He was promoted to Director of Guests; by regulation his marquisate was reduced to a viscountcy. He became Grand Palace Grandee and continued to handle the Bureau of Guests.
value.literal: He was promoted to Director of Guests; by regulation his marquisate was reduced to a viscountcy; he was transferred to Grand Palace Grandee and continued to handle the affairs of the Bureau of Guests.

value.zh: 尋為黃門。
value.en: Soon afterward he was made Superintendent of the Yellow Gate.
value.literal: Shortly afterward he became Superintendent of the Yellow Gate.

value.zh: 後從駕南征，母憂解任。
value.en: Later he accompanied the emperor on the southern campaign, then left office upon his mother's death.
value.literal: Later he accompanied the emperor on the southern campaign and resigned his post upon his mother's death.

value.zh: 彝居喪過禮，送葬自平城達家，千里徒步，不乘車馬，顏貌毀瘠，當世稱之。
value.en: Zhang Yi mourned beyond the prescribed rites. To escort the funeral from Pingcheng home—a thousand li—he went entirely on foot, never mounting horse or carriage. His face was wasted and gaunt, and his age praised him.
value.literal: Yi observed mourning beyond the prescribed rites; to escort the funeral from Pingcheng to his home he walked a thousand li on foot without riding horse or carriage; his appearance was gaunt and wasted—the age praised him for this.

value.zh: 高祖幸冀州，遣使弔慰，詔以驍騎將軍起之，還復本位。
value.en: When Emperor Wen visited Ji Province, he sent envoys to offer condolences and ordered Zhang Yi recalled as General of Valiant Cavalry. On his return he resumed his former post.
value.literal: Emperor Gaozu visited Ji Province, sent envoys to offer condolences, and ordered him recalled as General of Valiant Cavalry; upon return he resumed his former position.

value.zh: 以參定遷都之勳，進爵為侯，轉太常少卿，遷散騎常侍，兼侍中，持節巡察陝東、河南十二州，甚有聲稱。
value.en: For his merit in planning the move of the capital, he was raised to marquis, made Vice Director of the Grand Imperial Ancestral Temple, then Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrent Palace Attendant, bearing the staff to inspect the twelve provinces of Shaan East and Henan. His reputation soared.
value.literal: For his merit in participating in deciding the capital relocation, he was advanced to marquis, transferred to Vice Director of the Grand Imperial Ancestral Temple, promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Palace Attendant, bearing the staff to inspect the twelve provinces of Shaan East and Henan—his reputation was greatly enhanced.

value.zh: 使還，以從征之勤，遷尚書。
value.en: When he returned from his mission, he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Works for his service on campaign.
value.literal: Upon returning from his mission, for his diligence on the campaign he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Works.

value.zh: 坐舉元昭為兼郎中，黜為守尚書。
value.en: He was demoted to Acting Director of the Ministry of Works for recommending Yuan Zhao as concurrent Gentleman in the Secretariat.
value.literal: He was demoted to Acting Director of the Ministry of Works for having recommended Yuan Zhao as concurrent Gentleman in the Secretariat.

value.zh: 世宗初，除正尚書、兼侍中，尋正侍中。
value.en: At the start of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made full Director of the Ministry of Works and concurrent Palace Attendant, and soon afterward full Palace Attendant.
value.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, he was appointed full Director of the Ministry of Works and concurrent Palace Attendant; shortly afterward he became full Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 世宗親政，罷六輔，彝與兼尚書邢巒聞處分非常，出京奔走，為御史中尉甄琛所彈，云「非虎非兕，率彼曠野」，詔書切責之。
value.en: When Emperor Xuanwu took personal rule and dismissed the Six Assistants, Zhang Yi and Vice Director Xing Luan, hearing that extraordinary measures were afoot, fled the capital. Inspector-in-Chief Zhen Chen impeached them with the line "Neither tiger nor rhinoceros—driving through the open wild," and an imperial edict sharply rebuked them.
value.literal: When Emperor Shizong personally assumed government and dismissed the Six Assistants, Yi and Vice Director Xing Luan, hearing that the measures were extraordinary, fled the capital; they were impeached by the Inspector-in-Chief Zhen Chen, citing "Neither tiger nor rhinoceros—driving through the open wild," and an imperial edict sternly rebuked them.

value.zh: 尋除安西將軍、秦州刺史。
value.en: Soon afterward he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Qin Province.
value.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Qin Province.

value.zh: 彝務尚典式，考訪故事。
value.en: Zhang Yi devoted himself to proper forms and searched out precedent.
value.literal: Yi devoted himself to institutional forms and investigated precedents.

value.zh: 及臨隴右，彌加討習，於是出入直衞，方伯威儀，赫然可觀。
value.en: When he took up his post in Longyou, he applied himself all the more to study and drill. Whether entering or leaving, his guard escort and the bearing of a frontier governor were visibly imposing.
value.literal: When he arrived in Longyou [the west], he applied himself all the more to study and practice; thus whether entering or leaving, his imperial guard escort and the majesty of a regional governor were visibly imposing.

value.zh: 羌夏畏伏，憚其威整，一方肅靜，號為良牧。
value.en: The Qiang and Xia submitted in fear of his stern discipline. The region grew quiet, and he was hailed as an excellent governor.
value.literal: The Qiang and Xia peoples feared and submitted, dreading his stern authority; the region was tranquil and he was hailed as an excellent governor.

value.zh: 其年冬，太極初就，彝與郭祚等俱以勤舊被徵。
value.en: That winter, when the Taiji Palace was first completed, Zhang Yi and Guo Zuo and others were all summoned to court for their long service.
value.literal: That winter, when the Taiji Palace was first completed, Yi and Guo Zuo and others were all summoned for their long service and seniority.

value.zh: 及還州，進號撫軍將軍，彝表解州任，詔不許。
value.en: When he returned to his province his title was raised to General Who Pacifies the Army. Zhang Yi memorialized asking to resign the governorship, but the edict refused.
value.literal: When he returned to his province, his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army; Yi submitted a memorial requesting to relinquish his provincial post, but the edict did not permit it.

value.zh: 彝敷政隴右，多所制立，宣布新風，革其舊俗，民庶愛仰之。
value.en: In Longyou Zhang Yi governed broadly, establishing many new rules, proclaiming a new ethos and reforming old custom. The people loved and looked up to him.
value.literal: Yi spread good governance in Longyou, establishing many new regulations, proclaiming a new ethos and reforming old customs; the people loved and admired him.

value.zh: 為國造佛寺名曰興皇，諸有罪咎者，隨其輕重，謫為土木之功，無復鞭杖之罰。
value.en: For the state he built a Buddhist temple called Xinghuang. Offenders, according to the weight of their crimes, were assigned to construction labor instead of being flogged.
value.literal: He built for the state a Buddhist temple named Xinghuang; all who had offenses were, according to severity, relegated to labor on construction works, with no further flogging punishments.

value.zh: 時陳留公主寡居，彝意願尚主，主亦許之。
value.en: At that time the Princess of Chenliu was a widow. Zhang Yi wished to marry her, and the princess agreed.
value.literal: At that time the Princess of Chenliu was widowed; Yi wished to marry her, and the princess also agreed.

value.zh: 僕射高肇亦望尚主，主意不可。
value.en: Vice Director Gao Zhao also hoped to marry her, but the princess would not have it.
value.literal: Vice Director Gao Zhao also hoped to marry the princess, but the princess would not agree.

value.zh: 肇怒，譖彝於世宗，稱彝擅立刑法，勞役百姓。
value.en: Gao Zhao was furious and slandered Zhang Yi to Emperor Xuanwu, saying he had set up punishments on his own authority and overworked the people.
value.literal: Gao Zhao was enraged and slandered Yi to Emperor Shizong, claiming Yi had arbitrarily established penal laws and conscripted the people in labor.

value.zh: 詔遣直後萬貳興馳驛撿察。
value.en: An edict sent Direct Attendant Wan Erxing post-haste by relay to investigate.
value.literal: An edict dispatched the Direct Attendant Wan Erxing post-haste by relay to investigate.

value.zh: 貳興，肇所親愛，必欲致彝深罪。
value.en: Erxing was a man Gao Zhao favored and was bent on bringing Zhang Yi to ruin.
value.literal: Erxing was a man Gao Zhao cherished and favored; he was determined to bring deep guilt upon Yi.

value.zh: 彝清身奉法，求其愆過，遂無所得。
value.en: Zhang Yi had kept himself clean and upheld the law; they searched for fault and found none.
value.literal: Yi had kept himself pure and upheld the law; they sought his faults and ultimately found nothing.

value.zh: 見代還洛，猶停廢數年，因得偏風，手脚不便。
value.en: When his successor arrived he returned to Luoyang, but remained idle for several years. He then suffered a stroke and his hands and feet were impaired.
value.literal: When his replacement arrived he returned to Luoyang, yet remained idle and dismissed for several years; he thereupon contracted hemiplegia and his hands and feet were impaired.

value.zh: 然志性不移，善自將攝，稍能朝拜。
value.en: Yet his spirit did not change. He cared for himself well and gradually was able to attend court again.
value.literal: Yet his will and character did not change; he was good at caring for himself and gradually was able to attend court.

value.zh: 久之，除光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。
value.en: After a long while he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the gold seal and purple sash.
value.literal: After a long time, he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the gold seal and purple sash.

value.zh: 彝又表曰：「竊惟皇王統天，必以窮幽為美；
value.en: Zhang Yi submitted another memorial: "I believe that emperors who align with Heaven must regard penetrating the hidden as a virtue;
value.literal: Zhang Yi again memorialized: "I reflect that emperors and kings who harmonize with Heaven must take penetrating the obscure as excellence;

value.zh: 盡理作聖，亦假廣採成明。
value.en: To perfect understanding and become sage likewise depends on broad collection to achieve enlightenment.
value.literal: To exhaust principle and become sage likewise borrows broad collection to achieve clarity.

value.zh: 故詢於芻蕘，著之周什，輿人獻箴，流於夏典。
value.en: Hence inquiry was made even of grass cutters and recorded in the Zhou odes, and chariot makers offered admonitions preserved in the Xia canon.
value.literal: Therefore inquiry was made of grass cutters, recorded in the Odes of Zhou; chariot makers presented admonitions, flowing into the canon of Xia.

value.zh: 不然，則美刺無以得彰，善惡有時不達。
value.en: Otherwise praise and blame could never be made clear, and good and evil would sometimes never reach the ruler.
value.literal: Otherwise, praise and censure could not be made manifest, and good and evil would at times fail to reach [the throne].

value.zh: 逮於兩漢、魏、晉，雖道有隆汚，而被繡傳檄，未始闕也。
value.en: Down through the Two Han, Wei, and Jin, though governance rose and fell, officials in court dress presenting memorials never ceased.
value.literal: Reaching the Two Han, Wei, and Jin—though the Way had ascent and defilement—embroidered robes conveying memorials never once were lacking.

value.zh: 及惠帝失御，中夏崩離，劉苻專據秦西，燕趙獨制關左，姚夏繼起，五涼競立，致使九服搖搖，民無定主，禮儀典制，此焉堙滅。
value.en: When Emperor Hui lost the throne, the heartland fragmented; Liu and Fu held western Qin, Yan and Zhao controlled the eastern passes, Later Yan and the Five Liang rose in turn—the nine provinces trembled, the people had no settled ruler, and ritual and institutions perished.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui lost control, the Central Plains collapsed and split apart; Liu and Fu monopolized western Qin, Yan and Zhao alone controlled the passes to the left, Yao of Xia rose in succession, and the Five Liang competed to establish themselves—causing the nine domains to sway unsteadily, the people without a fixed lord, and ritual codes and institutions to be buried and extinguished here.

value.zh: 暨大魏應歷，撥亂登皇，翦彼鯨鯢，龕靖神縣，數紀之間，天下寧一，傳輝七帝，積聖如神。
value.en: When Northern Wei received the mandate, quelled chaos, and took the throne, it cut down its foes and restored order to the realm; within a few reigns the empire was unified, seven emperors passed down its glory, and sagacity accumulated like that of a spirit.
value.literal: When Great Wei received the mandate, quelling chaos and ascending the throne, cutting down those whale-demons and peacefully settling the divine counties, within a few reigns the realm was united under one rule, transmitting glory through seven emperors, accumulated sagacity like a spirit.

value.zh: 高祖遷鼎成周，永茲八百，偃武修文，憲章斯改，實所謂加五帝、登三王，民無德而名焉。
value.en: Emperor Gaozu moved the capital to Luoyang, continuing the Zhou legacy of eight hundred years, sheathed the sword and fostered letters, and reformed law and institutions—truly surpassing the Five Emperors and equaling the Three Kings, a fame the people need not ascribe to virtue alone.
value.literal: Emperor Gaozu moved the tripod to Cheng and Zhou, continuing those eight hundred years, laying down arms and cultivating culture, statutes and patterns thereby reformed—truly what is called surpassing the Five Emperors and ascending the Three Kings, the people without virtue yet naming it.

value.zh: 猶且慮獨見之不明，欲廣訪於得失，乃命四使，觀察風謠。
value.en: Yet he still feared that his own judgment alone might be unclear and wished to seek widely for what was right and wrong; he therefore appointed four envoys to observe folk songs and local opinion.
value.literal: Yet he still worried that solitary insight was not clear, and wished broadly to inquire into gains and losses; therefore he ordered four envoys to observe popular songs and rumors.

value.zh: 臣時忝常伯，充一使之列，遂得仗節揮金，宣恩東夏，周歷於齊魯之間，遍馳於梁宋之域，詢採詩頌，研撿獄情，實庶片言之不遺，美刺之俱顯。
value.en: I then served as Regular Grandee and was one of the four envoys; bearing the imperial staff I proclaimed grace in the east, traveled through Qi and Lu and across Liang and Song, gathered folk songs, and examined legal cases—hoping that no voice would be lost and that praise and blame alike would come to light.
value.literal: Your subject at the time held the post of Regular Grandee and filled one place among the envoys; thus I was able to bear the staff and wield gold, proclaiming grace in eastern Xia, touring between Qi and Lu, ranging widely through the lands of Liang and Song, inquiring into and collecting odes and hymns, examining and sorting prison cases—truly hoping that not a single word would be lost and that praise and censure alike would be displayed.

value.zh: 而才輕任重，多不遂心。
value.en: But my abilities were slight and my responsibilities heavy, and much did not go as I had hoped.
value.literal: Yet my talent was light and my burden heavy; much did not accord with my wishes.

value.zh: 所採之詩，並始申目，而值鑾輿南討，問罪宛鄧，臣復忝行軍，樞機是務。
value.en: The poems collected had only just been entered on the register when the emperor marched south to punish Wan and Deng; I was again attached to the campaign staff, occupied with military affairs.
value.literal: The odes collected had only just begun to be catalogued when the imperial carriage went south on campaign to question guilt at Wan and Deng; your subject again held a post on the campaign staff, with military keys as the task.

value.zh: 及輦駕之返，膳御未和，續以大諱奄臻，四海崩慕，遂爾推遷，不及聞徹。
value.en: When the emperor returned, the court was still in disarray; then came the sudden death of the emperor and universal mourning, and in the upheaval I never completed the submission.
value.literal: When the carriage returned, the imperial meals were not yet settled; continuing with the great bereavement suddenly arriving, the four seas collapsed in mourning; thus there was deferral and transfer, and I did not reach full report.

value.zh: 未幾，改牧秦蕃，違離闕下，繼以譴疾相纏，寧丁八歲。
value.en: Soon I was transferred to govern the Qin region, far from court; then reproof and illness followed one upon another, and I spent eight years in mourning for my father.
value.literal: Before long I was reassigned to govern the Qin frontier, parted from below the palace gates; continuing with reproof and illness entwined, I mourned for my father for eight years.

value.zh: 常恐所採之詩永淪丘壑，是臣夙夜所懷，以為深憂者也。
value.en: I constantly feared the poems I had gathered would be lost forever in obscurity—this has been my deepest worry night and day.
value.literal: I constantly feared the odes collected would forever sink into ravines and mounds—this is what your subject has harbored day and night, taking it as a deep worry.

value.zh: 陛下垂日月之明，行雲雨之施，察臣往罪之濫，矜臣貧病之切，既蒙崇以祿養，復得拜掃丘墳，明目友朋，無所負愧。
value.en: Your Majesty shines like sun and moon and showers grace like rain, overlooking my past excesses and pitying my poverty and illness; honored with stipends for my support and allowed again to tend my family's graves, I can face my friends without shame.
value.literal: Your Majesty sheds the brightness of sun and moon and exercises the bestowal of clouds and rain, examining the excess of your subject's past faults and pitying the urgency of my poverty and illness; having been honored with stipends for support, I was again able to sweep my ancestors' tombs—clear-eyed before friends, with nothing to bear as shame.

value.zh: 且臣一二年來，所患不劇，尋省本書，粗有髣髴。
value.en: Moreover, over the past year or two my illness has not been grave, and reviewing the original compilation I have recovered a rough draft.
value.literal: Moreover, for the past year or two my illness has not been severe; searching through the original book, there is a rough outline.

value.zh: 凡有七卷，今寫上呈，伏願昭覽，敕付有司，使魏代所採之詩，不堙於丘井，臣之願也。」
value.en: There are seven volumes in all, which I now submit; I humbly pray Your Majesty will review them and order the proper offices to preserve the poems gathered in the Wei period from being lost to oblivion—this is my sole wish."
value.literal: In all there are seven volumes; I now copy and present them above, humbly wishing Your Majesty would illuminate and view them and command the relevant offices, so that the odes collected in the Wei age may not be buried in wells and ravines—this is your subject's wish."

value.zh: 肅宗初，侍中崔光表曰：「彝及李韶，朝列之中唯此二人出身官次本在臣右，器能幹世，又並為多，近來參差，便成替後。
value.en: Early in Emperor Xiaoming's reign, Palace Attendant Cui Guang memorialized: "Zhang Yi and Li Shao are the only two men in court whose family standing and seniority originally ranked above mine, yet both are gifted administrators; recently, through uneven treatment, they have been passed over.
value.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign, Palace Attendant Cui Guang memorialized: "Yi and Li Shao—in the court ranks only these two men's origins and official seniority were originally above your subject's, yet in capacity and ability to govern the age they both excel; recently through uneven treatment they have been pushed to the rear.

value.zh: 計其階途，雖應遷陟，然恐班秩猶未賜等。
value.en: By the stages of their careers they ought to be promoted, yet I fear their ranks have still not been granted fairly.
value.literal: Calculating their stages of advancement, though they ought to be promoted and elevated, I fear their ranks and grades have still not been granted in equal measure.

value.zh: 昔衞之公叔，引下同舉；
value.en: In antiquity Wei's Gongsun drew up his subordinates to advance together;
value.literal: In former days the Gongsun of Wei drew up those below to advance together;

value.zh: 晉之士丐，推長伯游。
value.en: and Jin's Shigai promoted the senior Boyou.
value.literal: Jin's Shigai pushed forward the elder Boyou.

value.zh: 古人所高，當時見許。
value.en: What the ancients honored was praised and approved in their own day.
value.literal: What the ancients esteemed was praised and approved in their own time.

value.zh: 敢緣斯義，乞降臣位一階，授彼汎級，齊行聖庭，帖穆選敍。」
value.en: I venture to follow this principle and beg to lower my own rank by one step, granting them an equal grade so we may stand together at court in fair and harmonious order."
value.literal: I dare follow this principle and beg to lower my rank by one step, granting them a general grade, walking together in the sage court, harmoniously aligned in selection and ordering."

value.zh: 詔加征西將軍、冀州大中正。
value.en: An edict appointed him General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Rectifier of Ji Province.
value.literal: An edict appointed him General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Rectifier of Ji Province.

value.zh: 雖年向六十，加之風疾，而自強人事，孜孜無怠。
value.en: Though nearing sixty and afflicted with wind disorder, he still drove himself in public affairs, diligent and never slackening.
value.literal: Though he was nearing sixty and moreover afflicted with wind illness, he still forced himself in human affairs, diligent and never slackening.

value.zh: 公私法集，衣冠從事；
value.en: He compiled public and private law codes and gathered officials and gentry to assist;
value.literal: Public and private legal compilations, officials and gentry attending;

value.zh: 延請道俗，修營齋講；
value.en: invited Daoists and lay believers and organized fasts and lectures;
value.literal: inviting Daoists and lay believers, repairing and conducting fasts and lectures;

value.zh: 好善欽賢，愛獎人物。
value.en: loved the worthy, cherished talent, and rewarded men of ability.
value.literal: loving the good and respecting the worthy, cherishing and rewarding men of talent.

value.zh: 南北新舊莫不多之。
value.en: Men old and new, from north and south, all flocked to him.
value.literal: Whether from north or south, old or new, none failed to flock to him.

value.zh: 大起第宅，微號華侈，頗侮其疏宗舊戚，不甚存紀，時有怨憾焉。
value.en: He built grand mansions in a somewhat lavish style, showed little regard for distant clansmen and old kin, and at times stirred resentment.
value.literal: He greatly raised mansions and residences, slightly styled as splendid and extravagant, quite slighting his distant clansmen and old kin, not greatly preserving records of them; at times there were resentments.

value.zh: 榮宦之間，未能止足，屢表在秦州預有開援漢中之勳，希加賞報，積年不已，朝廷患之。
value.en: In his pursuit of rank he could not know when to stop; he repeatedly claimed credit for aiding the campaign to recover Hanzhong while governing Qinzhou and pressed for further rewards year after year until the court grew weary of it.
value.literal: Between glory and office he could not stop at sufficiency; repeatedly he memorialized that at Qinzhou he had beforehand rendered service in opening relief for Hanzhong, hoping for added reward and recompense, year after year without end—the court was troubled by it.

value.zh: 第二子仲瑀上封事，求銓別選格，排抑武人，不使預在清品。
value.en: His second son Zhongyu submitted a sealed memorial calling for revised selection standards that would exclude military men from the pure grades.
value.literal: His second son Zhongyu submitted a sealed memorial seeking to examine and separate selection standards, suppressing military men and not allowing them to enter the pure grades.

value.zh: 由是眾口喧喧，謗讟盈路，立榜大巷，剋期會集，屠害其家。
value.en: Because of this public outcry and slander filled the streets; placards were posted in the main thoroughfares fixing a date for assembly to attack his household.
value.literal: Because of this the multitude clamored, slander and abuse filled the roads; they posted placards in the great alleys, fixing a date to assemble, slaughtering and harming his household.

value.zh: 彝殊無畏避之意，父子安然。
value.en: Zhang Yi showed no fear or evasion; father and sons remained at ease.
value.literal: Yi showed absolutely no fear or avoidance; father and sons remained at ease.

value.zh: 神龜二年二月，羽林虎賁幾將千人，相率至尚書省詬罵，求其長子尚書郎始均，不獲，以瓦石擊打公門。
value.en: In the second month of the second Shengui year, nearly a thousand Feathered Forest and Tiger Guard soldiers went together to the Department of State Affairs to revile and abuse the family, seeking his eldest son Shijun, a Secretariat Gentleman; failing to find him, they pelted the ministry gates with tiles and stones.
value.literal: In the second month of the second year of Shengui, nearly a thousand Feathered Forest and Tiger Guard troops went together to the Department of State Affairs to revile and curse, seeking his eldest son, Secretariat Gentleman Shijun; not obtaining him, they struck the public gates with tiles and stones.

value.zh: 上下畏懼，莫敢討抑。
value.en: Officials high and low were terrified; none dared restrain them.
value.literal: High and low were fearful; none dared suppress or restrain them.

value.zh: 遂便持火，虜掠道中薪蒿，以杖石為兵器，直造其第，曳彝堂下，捶辱極意，唱呼嗸嗸，焚其屋宇。
value.en: They then seized fire, looted fuel along the road, took up staffs and stones as weapons, marched straight to his residence, dragged Zhang Yi into the courtyard, beat and humiliated him without restraint, shouting wildly as they burned his houses.
value.literal: They then took fire, plundering firewood and reeds along the road, using staffs and stones as weapons, going straight to his residence, dragging Yi beneath the hall, beating and humiliating him to the utmost, shouting and howling, burning his houses.

value.zh: 始均、仲瑀當時踰北垣而走。
value.en: Shijun and Zhongyu at once leaped the north wall and fled.
value.literal: Shijun and Zhongyu at the time leaped over the north wall and fled.

value.zh: 始均回救其父，拜伏羣小，以請父命。
value.en: Shijun turned back to save his father, prostrating himself before the mob to beg for his life.
value.literal: Shijun turned back to rescue his father, bowing prostrate before the mob to beg for his father's life.

value.zh: 羽林等就加毆擊，生投之於烟火之中。
value.en: The guards then beat him further and cast him alive into the fire and smoke.
value.literal: The Feathered Guard and others then added beating and strikes, casting him alive into the flames and smoke.

value.zh: 及得尸骸，不復可識，唯以髻中小釵為驗。
value.en: When his body was recovered it could no longer be identified; only a small hairpin in the topknot served to identify him.
value.literal: When the corpse was obtained it could no longer be recognized; only a small hairpin in the topknot served as identification.

value.zh: 仲瑀傷重走免。
value.en: Zhongyu, badly wounded, escaped.
value.literal: Zhongyu, severely wounded, fled and escaped.

value.zh: 彝僅有餘命，沙門寺與其比隣，輿致於寺。
value.en: Zhang Yi clung to life; a Buddhist monastery stood next door, and they carried him there on a litter.
value.literal: Yi had only a remnant of life; the Buddhist monastery neighbored him, and they carried him by litter to the monastery.

value.zh: 遠近聞見，莫不惋駭。
value.en: All who heard and saw it, near and far, were struck with grief and horror.
value.literal: Those near and far who heard and saw were all struck with grief and horror.

value.zh: 彝臨終，口占左右上啟曰：「臣自奉國及孫六世，尸祿素餐，負恩唯靦，徒思竭智盡誠，終然靡効。
value.en: On his deathbed Zhang Yi dictated a final memorial: "My family has served the state for six generations, receiving salary without merit and grace I have only shamed; I thought only to exhaust my loyalty, yet in the end achieved nothing.
value.literal: At the end of his life Yi dictated to those beside him a memorial above: "Your subject from serving the state through six generations has received salary without merit, bearing grace with only shame, merely thinking to exhaust wisdom and loyalty, yet in the end without effect.

value.zh: 臣第二息仲瑀所上之事，益治實多，既曰有益，寧容默爾。
value.en: The proposal my second son Zhongyu submitted would in truth benefit governance greatly; if it is beneficial, how could I keep silent?
value.literal: The matter submitted by your subject's second son Zhongyu in governing truly has much benefit; since it is said to be beneficial, how could it be silently tolerated?

value.zh: 通呈有日，未簡神聽，豈圖眾忿，乃至於此。
value.en: It had been submitted for days without yet reaching the emperor's ear; who could have imagined public fury would come to this?
value.literal: It had been presented for days without yet being sifted by the divine hearing; who would have thought popular wrath would reach this point?

value.zh: 臣不能禍防未萌，慮絕殃兆，致令軍眾橫囂，攻焚臣宅。
value.en: I could not forestall disaster before it sprouted or cut off the signs of calamity, and so soldiers rioted, attacked, and burned my house.
value.literal: Your subject could not ward off disaster before it sprouted, consider and cut off the omen of calamity, causing military masses to rampage and shout, attacking and burning your subject's residence.

value.zh: 息始均、仲瑀等叩請流血，乞代臣死，始均即陷塗炭，仲瑀經宿方蘇。
value.en: My sons Shijun and Zhongyu begged with blood flowing to die in my place; Shijun at once perished in the flames, and Zhongyu revived only after a night.
value.literal: My sons Shijun and Zhongyu knocked their heads and begged with flowing blood to die in my place; Shijun at once fell into ashes and charcoal, Zhongyu after a night barely revived.

value.zh: 臣年已六十，宿被榮遇，垂暮之秋，忽見此苦，顧瞻災酷，古今無比。
value.en: I am already sixty, long favored by the throne; in the autumn of my life I suddenly meet this agony—a cruelty without parallel in past or present.
value.literal: Your subject is already sixty years old, long receiving honored favor; in the autumn of life's decline I suddenly see this suffering; looking back on the cruel disaster, there is no parallel in past or present.

value.zh: 臣傷至重，殘氣假延，望景顧時，推漏就盡，頃刻待終，臣之命也，知復何言。
value.en: My wounds are grave; on borrowed breath I watch the shadow and count the hours, the water clock nearing its end, death imminent—this is my fate, and what more can I say?
value.literal: Your subject's wounds are extremely grave; with remnant breath borrowed for extension, looking at the shadow and counting the time, pushing the clepsydra toward its end, awaiting the final moment in an instant—your subject's fate; knowing again what to say.

value.zh: 若所上之書，少為益國，臣便是生以理全，死與義合，不負二帝於地下，臣無餘恨矣。
value.en: If what we submitted can even slightly benefit the state, then I have lived with integrity and die in righteousness, not failing the two emperors in the grave—I have no further regret.
value.literal: If the book submitted can slightly benefit the state, your subject would then be living with principle intact and dying united with righteousness, not failing the two emperors underground—your subject has no remaining regret.

value.zh: 一歸泉壤，長離紫庭，戀仰天顏，誠痛無已。
value.en: Once I return to the grave, forever parted from the imperial court, I shall still cherish Your Majesty's countenance—my grief will know no end.
value.literal: Once returning to the springs and mounds, long parted from the purple court, cherishing and looking up at the heavenly countenance, truly pain without end.

value.zh: 不勝眷眷，力喘奉辭，伏願二聖加御珍膳，覆露黔首，壽保南嶽，德與日昇。
value.en: Overcome with devotion, gasping out these words I take leave; I humbly pray the two sovereigns will guard their precious health, shelter the common people, long preserve life as the southern mountains, and let virtue rise with the sun.
value.literal: Unable to bear the deep attachment, with strength gasping I offer this farewell; humbly wishing the two sages would add to their precious meals, cover and shelter the black-haired people, preserve life like the southern mountains, virtue rising with the sun.

value.zh: 臣夙被芻豢，先後銜恩，欲報之期，昊天罔極，亡魂有知，不忘結草。」
value.en: I have long been fed by the state's bounty and repeatedly received grace; the time to repay is boundless as Heaven—if my departed soul has awareness, I shall not forget to repay with knotted grass."
value.literal: Your subject long received fodder and grain, successively bearing grace; the time to repay is boundless as Heaven—if the departed soul has awareness, I shall not forget the knotted grass."

value.zh: 彝遂卒，時年五十九。
value.en: Zhang Yi then died at the age of fifty-nine.
value.literal: Zhang Yi then died, aged fifty-nine at the time.

value.zh: 官為收掩羽林凶強者八人斬之，不能窮誅羣豎，即為大赦以安眾心，有識者知國紀之將墜矣。
value.en: The authorities buried Zhang Yi and beheaded eight of the ringleaders among the guards but could not punish the whole mob; a general amnesty was then issued to calm the people—those with insight knew the dynasty's discipline was collapsing.
value.literal: The government for collecting and burying beheaded eight of the violent among the Feathered Guard but could not exhaustively punish the whole mob; thereupon a great amnesty was issued to settle popular hearts—those with insight knew the nation's discipline was about to fall.

value.zh: 喪還所焚宅，與始均東西分斂於小屋。
value.en: The funeral procession returned to the burned house; Zhang Yi and Shijun were laid out separately in a small room east and west.
value.literal: The funeral returned to the burned residence; east and west with Shijun they were separately enshrouded in a small room.

value.zh: 仲瑀遂以創重避居滎陽，至五月，創得漸瘳，始奔父喪，詔賜布帛千匹。
value.en: Zhongyu, severely wounded, took refuge at Xingyang; by the fifth month his wounds had healed enough for him to attend his father's funeral, and an edict granted him a thousand bolts of cloth and silk.
value.literal: Zhongyu then because of severe wounds avoided residence at Xingyang; by the fifth month the wounds gradually healed and he first rushed to his father's funeral; an edict bestowed a thousand bolts of cloth and silk.

value.zh: 靈太后以其累朝大臣，特垂矜惻，數月猶追言泣下，謂諸侍臣曰：「吾為張彝飲食不御，乃至首髮微有虧落。
value.en: Empress Dowager Ling, because he had served many reigns, showed special compassion; for months she still spoke of him in tears, telling the attendant ministers: "For Zhang Yi I have refused my meals, even until the hair on my head has begun to thin.
value.literal: Empress Dowager Ling, because he was a minister of many reigns, especially showed pity; for months she still spoke of it with tears, saying to the attendant ministers: "Because of Zhang Yi I have not taken my meals, even to the point that the hair on my head has slightly fallen out.

value.zh: 悲痛之苦，以至於此。」
value.en: My grief has gone as far as this."
value.literal: The pain of grief has reached this point."

value.zh: 初，彝曾祖幸，所招引河東民為州裁千餘家，後相依合，至於罷入冀州，積三十年，析別有數萬戶，故高祖比校天下民戶，最為大州。
value.en: Earlier, Zhang Yi's great-grandfather Xing had settled more than a thousand households from Hedong in the province; over thirty years they grew through division and merger to tens of thousands of households—so when Emperor Gaozu compared household registers throughout the realm, Ji ranked as the largest province.
value.literal: Earlier, Yi's great-grandfather Xing had attracted and settled over a thousand households of Hedong people as provincial settlers; later they joined together, until dismissal and entry into Ji Province, accumulating thirty years; through division and separation there were tens of thousands of households—therefore Emperor Gaozu compared and checked the realm's household registers and [Ji] was the greatest province.

value.zh: 彝為黃門，每侍坐以為言，高祖謂之曰：「終當以卿為刺史，酬先世誠效。」
value.en: When Zhang Yi served as Attendant of the Yellow Gate, he raised the matter whenever he attended the emperor, who told him: "In the end I shall make you inspector to reward your ancestors' loyal service."
value.literal: When Yi was Attendant of the Yellow Gate, each time he sat in attendance he spoke of this; Emperor Gaozu said to him: "In the end I shall take you as inspector to reward your forebears' sincere service."

value.zh: 彝追高祖往旨，累乞本州，朝議未許。
value.en: Zhang Yi pressed the emperor's earlier promise and repeatedly begged for his home province, but court deliberation did not approve.
value.literal: Yi pursued Emperor Gaozu's former intent and repeatedly begged for his native province; court deliberation did not permit it.

value.zh: 彝亡後，靈太后云：「彝屢乞冀州，吾欲用之，有人違我此意。
value.en: After Zhang Yi's death, Empress Dowager Ling said: "Zhang Yi repeatedly asked for Ji Province; I meant to grant it—someone opposed my wish.
value.literal: After Yi died, Empress Dowager Ling said: "Yi repeatedly begged for Ji Province; I wished to use him—someone went against my intent in this.

value.zh: 若從其請，或不至是，悔之無及。」
value.en: Had I granted his request, perhaps things would not have come to this—my regret is boundless."
value.literal: If I had followed his request, perhaps it would not have come to this; regret is without limit."

value.zh: 乃贈使持節、衞將軍、冀州刺史，諡文侯。
value.en: He was then posthumously honored as Bearer of the Staff, Defender General, and Inspector of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Marquis Wen.
value.literal: Thereupon he was posthumously awarded Bearer of the Staff, Defender General, and Inspector of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Marquis Wen.

value.zh: 始均，字子衡，端潔好學，有文才。
value.en: Shijun, whose courtesy name was Ziheng, was upright, pure, and fond of learning, with literary gifts.
value.literal: Shijun, courtesy name Ziheng, was upright, pure, and fond of learning, with literary talent.

value.zh: 司徒行參軍，遷著作佐郎。
value.en: He served as staff officer to the Grand Commandant and was promoted to Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library.
value.literal: Staff Officer of the Grand Commandant, promoted to Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library.

value.zh: 世宗以彝先朝勤舊，不幸疹廢，特除始均長兼左民郎中。
value.en: Emperor Xuanwu, because Zhang Yi was a meritorious minister of the previous reign who had met a tragic end, specially appointed Shijun as long-term concurrent Left Gentleman of the Ministry of the People.
value.literal: Emperor Shizong, because Yi was an old meritorious minister of the former court who had met misfortune and ruin, specially appointed Shijun long-term concurrent Left Gentleman of the Ministry of the People.

value.zh: 遷員外常侍，仍領郎。
value.en: He was promoted to Supernumerary Palace Attendant while retaining his gentleman post.
value.literal: Promoted to Supernumerary Palace Attendant, still holding the gentleman post.

value.zh: 始均才幹，有美於父，改陳壽魏志為編年之體，廣益異聞，為三十卷。
value.en: Shijun's ability surpassed his father's; he reworked Chen Shou's Records of Wei into annalistic form, adding much additional material, in thirty volumes.
value.literal: Shijun's talent and ability had beauty surpassing his father; he revised Chen Shou's Records of Wei into annalistic form, broadly adding divergent hearsay, making thirty volumes.

value.zh: 又著冠帶錄及諸賦數十篇，今並亡失。
value.en: He also wrote Record of Caps and Belts and several dozen fu rhapsodies; all are now lost.
value.literal: He also composed Record of Caps and Belts and several dozen fu rhapsodies; all are now lost.

value.zh: 初，大乘賊起於冀瀛之間，遣都督元遙討平之，多所殺戮，積尸數萬。
value.en: Earlier, Mahayana rebels rose in the Ji and Ying region; Commander Yuan Yao was dispatched to suppress them, killing many until corpses numbered in the tens of thousands.
value.literal: Initially Mahayana rebels arose between Ji and Ying; Commander Yuan Yao was dispatched to suppress and pacify them, killing many until corpses piled up to tens of thousands.

value.zh: 始均以郎中為行臺，忿軍士重以首級為功，乃令檢集人首數千，一時焚爇，至於灰燼，用息僥倖，見者莫不傷心。
value.en: As a director on the campaign staff, Shijun was angered that soldiers prized enemy heads for merit; he had thousands of heads gathered and burned to ash at once to curb opportunism, and all who saw it were heartsick.
value.literal: Shijun served as Gentleman on the mobile secretariat; angered that the soldiers prized enemy heads for merit, he ordered thousands of human heads collected and burned at once to ashes, to quell opportunism—all who witnessed it were grieved.

value.zh: 及始均之死也，始末在於烟炭之間，有燋爛之痛，論者或亦推咎焉。
value.en: When Shijun died, he had been caught from start to finish in smoke and fire, burned alive—some commentators blamed his earlier act for it.
value.literal: When Shijun died, from beginning to end he was amid smoke and embers, suffering the pain of scorching—commentators sometimes placed blame on this as well.

value.zh: 贈樂陵太守，諡曰孝。
value.en: He was posthumously made Administrator of Laoling, with the posthumous name Xiao.
value.literal: He was posthumously granted Administrator of Laoling, with the posthumous name Xiao.

value.zh: 儒學上
value.en: Confucian Scholars, Part One
value.literal: Confucian Scholars, Part One

value.zh: 孫齊丘，歷監察御史、朔方節度使，終東都留守，謚曰貞獻。
value.en: His grandson Qiqiu successively served as Censor, Military Commissioner of Shuofang, and ended as Guardian of the Eastern Capital, his posthumous title was Zhenxian.
value.literal: His grandson Qiqiu successively served as Censor, Military Commissioner of Shuofang, and ended as Guardian of the Eastern Capital; his posthumous title was Zhenxian.

value.zh: 子鎰，別有傳。
value.en: His son Yi is treated in a separate biography.
value.literal: His son Yi has a separate biography.

value.zh: 十九年春正月壬戌朔，高麗國王王春遣其大將軍金子廷來賀。
value.en: In the nineteenth year, on the renxu new moon of the first month of spring, King Wang Chun of Goryeo sent his general-in-chief Jin Ziting to offer congratulations.
