value.literal: In the nineteenth year, spring, first month, on the renxu new moon, King Wang Chun of Goryeo dispatched his general-in-chief Jin Ziting to offer congratulations.

value.zh: 丙寅，罷征東行中書省。
value.en: On bingyin day the Japan expedition branch secretariat was abolished.
value.literal: On bingyin day the Japan Expedition Branch Secretariat was abolished.

value.zh: 丁卯，諸王劄剌忽至自軍中。
value.en: On dingmao day Prince Zhalahu arrived from the army.
value.literal: On dingmao day Prince Zhalahu arrived from the army.

value.zh: 時皇子北平王以軍鎮阿裏麻裏之地，以禦海都。
value.en: At that time the imperial son, Prince of Beiping, had troops garrison Alimali to guard against Kaidu.
value.literal: At that time the imperial son, Prince of Beiping, had troops garrison the land of Alimali to guard against Kaidu.

value.zh: 諸王昔裏吉與脫脫木兒、棨木忽兒、撒裏蠻等謀劫皇子北平王以叛，欲與劄剌忽結援於海都，海都不從。
value.en: Prince Sheraqi, together with Tuotuo Mier, Qimuhuer, Sariman, and others, plotted to seize the Prince of Beiping and rebel, hoping to ally through Zhalahu with Kaidu; Kaidu refused.
value.literal: Prince Sheraqi, together with Tuotuo Mier, Qimuhuer, Sariman, and others, plotted to seize the Prince of Beiping and rebel, wishing to link arms through Zhalahu with Kaidu; Kaidu would not agree.

value.zh: 撒裏蠻悔過，執昔裏吉等，北平王遣劄剌忽以聞。
value.en: Sariman repented, seized Sheraqi and the others, and the Prince of Beiping sent Zhalahu to report it.
value.literal: Sariman repented, seized Sheraqi and the others, and the Prince of Beiping sent Zhalahu to report it.

value.zh: 妖民張圓光伏誅。
value.en: The sorcerer-subversive Zhang Roundong was executed.
value.literal: The sorcerer-subversive Zhang Roundong was executed.

value.zh: 立太僕院。
value.en: The Grand Stable Office was established.
value.literal: The Grand Stable Office was established.

value.zh: 撥信州民四百八戶隸諸王柏木兒。
value.en: 408 Xinzhou households were assigned to Prince Bomuer.
value.literal: Four hundred eight Xinzhou households were assigned to Prince Bomuer.

value.zh: 丙子，車駕畋於近郊。
value.en: On bingzi day the imperial carriage hunted near the capital.
value.literal: On bingzi day the imperial carriage hunted in the near suburbs.

value.zh: 丁丑，高麗國王貢綢布四百匹。
value.en: On dingchou day the king of Goryeo presented 400 bolts of silk cloth as tribute.
value.literal: On dingchou day the king of Goryeo presented four hundred bolts of silk cloth as tribute.

value.zh: 丙戌，賜西平王怯薛那懷等鈔一萬一千五百二十一錠。
value.en: On bingxu day Keshig Naqun, Prince of Xiping, and others were granted 11,521 ingots of paper currency.
value.literal: On bingxu day Keshig Naqun, Prince of Xiping, and others were granted eleven thousand five hundred twenty-one ingots of paper currency.

value.zh: 三月辛酉朔，烏蒙民叛，敕那懷、火魯思迷率蒙古、漢人新附軍討之。
value.en: In the third month, on the xinyou new moon, Wumeng people rebelled; an edict ordered Naqun and Qorqas Timish to lead Mongol and newly submitted Han troops to suppress them.
value.literal: Third month, on the xinyou new moon, Wumeng people rebelled; an edict ordered Naqun and Qorqas Timish to lead Mongol and newly submitted Han troops to suppress them.

value.zh: 賞忽都答兒等戰功牛羊馬。
value.en: Cattle, sheep, and horses were granted to reward the battle merit of Qutuq Dar and others.
value.literal: Cattle, sheep, and horses were granted to reward the battle merit of Qutuq Dar and others.

value.zh: 益都千戶王著，以阿合馬蠹國害民，與高和尚合謀殺之。
value.en: Yidu qianhu Wang Zhu, because Ahmad had corrupted the state and harmed the people, joined Gao Heshang in a plot to kill him.
value.literal: Yidu qianhu Wang Zhu, because Ahmad had corrupted the state and harmed the people, joined Gao Heshang in a plot to kill him.

value.zh: 壬午，誅王著、張易、高和尚於市，皆醢之，余黨悉伏誅。
value.en: On renwu day Wang Zhu, Zhang Yi, and Gao Heshang were executed in the market and their bodies pickled; all remaining accomplices were executed.
value.literal: On renwu day Wang Zhu, Zhang Yi, and Gao Heshang were executed in the market, all pickled; remaining accomplices were entirely executed.

value.zh: 甲申，的斤帖林以己貲充屯田之費，諸王阿只吉以聞，敕酬其直。
value.en: On jiashen day Dejin Telin used his own funds for garrison-farm expenses; Prince Ajiji reported it; an edict compensated him at fair value.
value.literal: On jiashen day Dejin Telin used his own funds for garrison-farm expenses; Prince Ajiji reported it; an edict compensated him at fair value.

value.zh: 丙戌，禁益都、東平、沿淮諸郡軍民官捕獵。
value.en: On bingxu day hunting by military and civilian officials of Yidu, Dongping, and commanderies along the Huai was forbidden.
value.literal: On bingxu day hunting by military and civilian officials of Yidu, Dongping, and commanderies along the Huai was forbidden.

value.zh: 戊子，立塔兒八合你驛，以烏蒙阿謀歲輸騬馬給之。
value.en: On wuzi day Tatarbaqani Station was established, supplied annually with gelded horses from Wumeng Amu.
value.literal: On wuzi day Tatarbaqani Station was established, supplied annually with gelded horses from Wumeng Amu.

value.zh: 以領北庭都護阿必失哈為御史大夫，行御史臺事。
value.en: Beshbaligh protector-general Abishaq was made censor-in-chief, conducting branch censorate affairs.
value.literal: Beshbaligh protector-general Abishaq was made censor-in-chief, conducting branch censorate affairs.

value.zh: 安童，木華黎四世孫，霸突魯長子也。
value.en: Antong, a fourth-generation descendant of Muqali, was the eldest son of Batu.
value.literal: Antong was a fourth-generation descendant of Muqali and the eldest son of Batu.

value.zh: 中統初，世祖追錄元勳，召入長宿衛，年方十三，位在百僚上。
value.en: Early in the Zhongtong reign, Kublai posthumously recognized the founding merits of his forebears and summoned Antong into the permanent palace guard. Though only thirteen, he already stood above the entire bureaucracy.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Zhongtong era, the Shizu Emperor posthumously honored the founding merits and summoned him into the permanent palace guard; he was only thirteen, yet ranked above all officials.

value.zh: 母弘吉剌氏，昭睿皇后之姊，通籍禁中。
value.en: His mother belonged to the Hongjila Kereit clan, was the elder sister of Empress Zhaorui, and was registered to reside within the inner palace.
value.literal: His mother was of the Hongjila Kereit clan, elder sister of Empress Zhaorui, and held registered residence in the inner palace.

value.zh: 世祖一日見之，問及安童，對曰：「安童雖幼，公輔器也。」
value.en: One day Kublai saw her and inquired about Antong. She answered, "Young as Antong is, he has the makings of a chief minister."
value.literal: One day the Shizu Emperor saw her and asked about Antong; she replied, "Although Antong is young, he has the makings of a chief minister."

value.zh: 世祖曰：「何以知之。」
value.en: The emperor asked, "How do you know that?"
value.literal: The emperor said, "How do you know this?"

value.zh: 對曰：「每退朝必與老成人語，未嘗狎一年少，是以知之。」
value.en: She said, "After every audience he talks with seasoned elders and never keeps company with the young—that is how I know."
value.literal: She replied, "Whenever he leaves court he speaks with elderly men of experience and never keeps company with the young, and that is how I know."

value.zh: 世祖悅。
value.en: Kublai was pleased.
value.literal: The emperor was pleased.

value.zh: 李璮反山東，事連王文統，平章趙璧素忌希憲勳名，因言文統由張易、希憲薦引，遂至大用，且關中形勝之地，希憲得民心，有商挺、趙良弼為之輔，此事宜關聖慮。
value.en: When Li Tan rebelled in Shandong, the affair implicated Wang Wentong. Grand Councillor Zhao Bi, who had long resented Lian Xixian's fame, said Wentong had risen through recommendations by Zhang Yi and Lian Xixian, that Lian Xixian held the strategic Guanzhong region and had won popular loyalty with Shang Ting and Zhao Liangbi as his aides—matters that should concern the throne.
value.literal: Li Tan rebelled in Shandong and the affair implicated Wang Wentong. The Grand Councillor Zhao Bi had long resented Lian Xixian's merit and fame and therefore said that Wentong had been recommended and introduced by Zhang Yi and Lian Xixian and thus came to great employment, and moreover that in the strategically advantageous land of Guanzhong Lian Xixian had won the people's hearts, with Shang Ting and Zhao Liangbi as his assistants—this matter should concern the sage's consideration.

value.zh: 帝曰：「希憲自幼事朕，朕知其心，挺、良弼皆正士，何慮焉。」
value.en: The Emperor said, "Lian Xixian has served me since youth and I know his heart. Ting and Liangbi are both upright men—what is there to fear?"
value.literal: The Emperor said, "Lian Xixian has served me since youth and I know his heart. Ting and Liangbi are both upright men—what is there to worry about?"

value.zh: 蜀降人費正寅以私怨譖希憲因李璮叛，亦修城治兵，潛畜異志，帝因惑之，命中書右丞南合代希憲行省，且覆視所告事，卒無實狀。
value.en: A surrendered Shu man, Fei Zhengyin, slandered Lian Xixian out of private spite, claiming that amid Li Tan's rebellion he too was fortifying cities, drilling troops, and harboring secret ambitions. The Emperor was unsettled and ordered Right Vice Director Nanhe to replace him in provincial administration and reinvestigate the charges. In the end nothing was substantiated.
value.literal: A surrendered man of Shu, Fei Zhengyin, slandered Lian Xixian out of private resentment, saying that because of Li Tan's rebellion he too was repairing walls and training troops and secretly harbored a contrary intent. The Emperor was thereby misled and ordered the Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Nanhe to replace Lian Xixian in provincial administration and moreover reinvestigate the reported matters. In the end there was no substantiating evidence.

value.zh: 詔希憲還京師，陛見，言曰：「方關陝叛亂，川蜀未寧，事急星火，臣隨宜行事，不謀佐貳，如寅所言，罪止在臣，臣請逮繫有司。」
value.en: An edict recalled Lian Xixian to the capital. At audience he said, "When Guan-Shaan was in rebellion and Sichuan unsettled, affairs were urgent as fire. I acted as circumstances required without consulting colleagues. If Zhengyin's charges hold, guilt rests on me alone—I ask to be handed over to the authorities."
value.literal: An edict ordered Lian Xixian back to the capital. At audience he said, "Just when Guan and Shaan were in rebellion and Chuan and Shu were not yet settled, affairs were urgent as sparks and fire. Your servant acted as circumstances required without consulting a second adviser. As Zhengyin said, guilt rests only on your servant. I request to be seized and handed to the responsible offices."

value.zh: 帝撫御床曰：「當時之言，天知之，朕知之，卿果何罪！」
value.en: The Emperor stroked the imperial couch and said, "Heaven knows what you did then, and so do I—what crime have you truly committed!"
value.literal: The Emperor stroked the imperial couch and said, "What was said at the time—Heaven knows it, I know it—what crime do you truly have!"

value.zh: 慰諭良久。
value.en: He comforted and reassured him at length.
value.literal: He comforted and instructed him at length.

value.zh: 進拜中書平章政事。
value.en: He was promoted to Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.
value.literal: He was advanced to Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 一日夜半，召希憲入禁中，從容道藩邸時事，因及趙璧所言。
value.en: One night at midnight he summoned Lian Xixian into the inner palace, spoke at ease of affairs from the princely years, and brought up what Zhao Bi had said.
value.literal: One day at midnight he summoned Lian Xixian into the inner palace, spoke at ease of affairs in the princely establishment, and thereby touched on what Zhao Bi had said.

value.zh: 希憲曰：「昔攻鄂時，賈似道作木柵環城，一夕而成，陛下顧扈從諸臣曰『吾安得如似道者用之』。
value.en: Lian Xixian said, "During the attack on Ezhou, Jia Sidao built wooden palisades around the city wall in a single night. Your Majesty turned to your attendants and said, 'How might I find and employ someone like Sidao?'
value.literal: Lian Xixian said, "In the past when attacking Ezhou, Jia Sidao built wooden palisades encircling the city wall, completed in a single night. Your Majesty turned to the various ministers in attendance and said, 'How might I obtain and employ someone like Sidao?'

value.zh: 劉秉忠、張易進曰『山東王文統，才智士也。
value.en: Liu Bingzhong and Zhang Yi stepped forward and said, 'Wang Wentong of Shandong is a man of talent and wisdom.'
value.literal: Liu Bingzhong and Zhang Yi advanced and said, 'Wang Wentong of Shandong is a man of talent and wisdom.'

value.zh: 今為李璮幕僚』。
value.en: He is now on Li Tan's staff.'
value.literal: He is now a staff officer of Li Tan.'

value.zh: 詔問臣，臣對『亦聞之，實未嘗識其人也』。」
value.en: Your Majesty asked me, and I replied, 'I too have heard of him, but I have never actually known the man.'"
value.literal: Your Majesty questioned your servant, and your servant replied, 'I too have heard of him, but in truth I have never known the man.'"

value.zh: 帝曰：「朕亦記此。」
value.en: The Emperor said, "I remember that as well."
value.literal: The Emperor said, "I too remember this."

value.zh: 五月，至上都，太常卿田忠良來問疾，希憲謂曰：「上都，聖上龍飛之地，天下視為根本近聞龍岡遺火，延燒民居，此常事耳，慎勿令妄談地理者惑動上意。」
value.en: In the fifth month he reached Shangdu. Tian Zhongliang, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, came to inquire after his health. Lian Xixian told him, "Shangdu is where the Emperor rose to power—the realm regards it as the foundation. I have lately heard that stray fire at Dragon Mound spread to burn common dwellings. That is an ordinary matter. Be careful not to let geomancers who talk recklessly of fate sway the Emperor's mind."
value.literal: In the fifth month he reached Shangdu. Taichangqing Tian Zhongliang came to inquire after his illness. Lian Xixian told him, "Shangdu is where the Sage ascended as dragon—the realm views it as root and foundation. Recently I heard Dragon Mound had stray fire spreading to burn common dwellings—this is an ordinary matter. Be careful not to let those who recklessly discuss geomancy stir the Emperor's mind."

value.zh: 未幾，果有數輩以徙置都邑事奏，樞密副使張易、中書左丞張文謙與之廷辨，力言不可，帝不悅。
value.en: Before long, several officials did indeed memorialize on moving the capital. Privy Council Vice Commissioner Zhang Yi and Secretariat Left Assistant Zhang Wenqian argued against them in open court, insisting it must not be done. Kublai was displeased.
value.literal: Before long, indeed several people memorialized on relocating the capital city. Privy Council Vice Commissioner Zhang Yi and Secretariat Left Assistant Zhang Wenqian disputed with them in court, strenuously saying it could not be done—the Emperor was displeased.

value.zh: 明日，召忠良質其事，忠良以希憲語對，帝曰：「希憲病甚，猶慮及此耶。」
value.en: The next day Kublai summoned Zhongliang to question him about the matter. Zhongliang repeated Lian Xixian's words. Kublai said, "Lian Xixian is gravely ill—he still worries about this?"
value.literal: The next day the Emperor summoned Zhongliang to verify the affair; Zhongliang answered with Lian Xixian's words. The Emperor said, "Lian Xixian is gravely ill—he still worries to this point?"

value.zh: 其議遂止。
value.en: The proposal was dropped.
value.literal: That proposal was thereby stopped.

value.zh: 賀仁傑
value.en: He Renjie
value.literal: He Renjie

value.zh: 高觿，字彥解，渤海人。
value.en: Gao Xi, whose style name was Yanjie, was a native of Bohai.
value.literal: Gao Xi, styled Yanjie, was a man of Bohai.

value.zh: 世仕金，祖彝，徙居上黨。
value.en: His family had served the Jin for generations. His grandfather Yi relocated to Shangdang.
value.literal: His family served Jin for generations; his grandfather Yi moved to reside in Shangdang.

value.zh: 父守忠，國初為千戶。
value.en: His father Shouzhong was a chiliarch in the early years of the dynasty.
value.literal: His father Shouzhong was a chiliarch at the beginning of the dynasty.

value.zh: 太宗九年，從親王口溫不花攻黃州，歿於兵。
value.en: In the ninth year of Taizong's reign he followed Prince Köten in the attack on Huangzhou and died in battle.
value.literal: In the ninth year of Taizong he followed Prince Köten in attacking Huangzhou and died in battle.

value.zh: 觿事世祖，備宿衛，頗見親幸。
value.en: Xi served Kublai in the palace guard and enjoyed considerable favor.
value.literal: Xi served the Founder, stood ready in the palace guard, and was rather favored.

value.zh: 至元初，立燕王為皇太子，詔選才雋士充官屬，以觿掌藝文，兼領中醖、宮衛監門事，又監作皇太子宮，規制有法，帝嘉之，錫以金幣、厩馬，因賜名失剌。
value.en: Early in the Zhiyuan era the Prince of Yan was made crown prince, and talented scholars were selected for his staff. Xi was put in charge of literary affairs, concurrently headed central brewing and palace gatekeeping, and supervised construction of the crown prince's palace with sound regulations. The emperor was pleased, granted him gold and currency and stable horses, and gave him the name Shila.
value.literal: At the beginning of Zhiyuan the Prince of Yan was established as crown prince; an edict selected talented scholars to fill his staff; Xi was put in charge of literary arts, concurrently headed central brewing and palace gate guard affairs, and also supervised construction of the crown prince's palace with regulated standards; the emperor praised this and granted gold and currency and stable horses, thereby granting the name Shila.

value.zh: 十八年，授中議大夫、工部侍郎，行同知王府都總管府事。
value.en: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Grand Master of Correct Counsel and vice minister of Works, acting associate director of the crown prince's chief steward's office.
value.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Grand Master of Correct Counsel and vice minister of Works, acting associate director of the crown prince's chief steward's office.

value.zh: 十九年春，皇太子從帝北幸。
value.en: In the spring of the nineteenth year the crown prince accompanied the emperor on the northern progress.
value.literal: In spring of the nineteenth year the crown prince followed the emperor on the northern progress.

value.zh: 時丞相阿合馬留守大都，專權貪恣，人厭苦之。
value.en: Chief Councillor Ahmad remained at Daidu, monopolizing power in greed and arrogance until the people were weary of his rule.
value.literal: At that time Chief Councillor Ahmad remained at Daidu, monopolizing power and greedy and unrestrained; people were weary and suffering under him.

value.zh: 益都千戶王著與高和尚等，因構變謀殺之。
value.en: Wang Zhu, a chiliarch of Yidu, joined Gaoshanghe and others in a plot to murder him.
value.literal: Yidu chiliarch Wang Zhu and Gaoshanghe and others therefore plotted a disturbance to murder him.

value.zh: 三月十七日，觿宿衛宮中，西蕃僧二人至中書省，言今夕皇太子與國師來建佛事。
value.en: On the seventeenth day of the third month Xi was on guard in the palace when two Tibetan monks came to the Secretariat and said the crown prince and the imperial preceptor would come that evening to perform Buddhist rites.
value.literal: On the seventeenth day of the third month Xi was on guard in the palace; two Western Tibetan monks came to the Secretariat saying that this evening the crown prince and the imperial preceptor would come to perform Buddhist rites.

value.zh: 省中疑之，俾嘗出入東宮者雜識視之，觿等皆莫識也，乃作西蕃語詢二僧曰：「皇太子及國師今至何處？」
value.en: The Secretariat was suspicious and had men who knew the Eastern Palace staff examine them. Xi and the others recognized none of them. Xi questioned the monks in Tibetan: "Where are the crown prince and the imperial preceptor now?"
value.literal: Those in the Secretariat were suspicious and had those who had gone in and out of the Eastern Palace mixed among them to look; Xi and the others all failed to recognize them, and therefore spoke in Western Tibetan to question the two monks: "Where have the crown prince and imperial preceptor arrived now?"

value.zh: 二僧失色。
value.en: The two monks turned pale.
value.literal: The two monks changed color.

value.zh: 又以漢語詰之，倉皇莫能對，遂執二僧屬吏。
value.en: He questioned them again in Chinese. Flustered, they could not answer, and the two monks were seized and handed over to the authorities.
value.literal: He again questioned them in Chinese; flustered they could not answer, and the two monks were seized and handed to officials.

value.zh: 訊之皆不伏，觿恐有變，乃與尚書忙兀兒、張九思集衛士及官兵，各執弓矢以備。
value.en: Under interrogation they confessed nothing. Fearing a disturbance, Xi joined Ministers Mangwuer and Zhang Jiusi in gathering palace guards and government troops, all armed with bows and arrows.
value.literal: Under interrogation none confessed; Xi feared a disturbance and therefore joined with Ministers Mangwuer and Zhang Jiusi to gather guards and government troops, each holding bow and arrows in readiness.

value.zh: 頃之，樞密副使張易亦領兵駐宮外。
value.en: Shortly afterward Privy Council vice director Zhang Yi also led troops and encamped outside the palace.
value.literal: Shortly after, Privy Council Vice Director Zhang Yi also led troops stationed outside the palace.

value.zh: 觿問：「果何為？」
value.en: Xi asked, "What is really going on?"
value.literal: Xi asked: "What is really happening?"

value.zh: 易曰：「夜後當自見。」
value.en: Yi said, "You will see for yourself after nightfall."
value.literal: Yi said: "After nightfall you will see for yourself."

value.zh: 觿固問，乃附耳語曰：「皇太子來誅阿合馬也。」
value.en: When Xi pressed him, Yi whispered in his ear, "The crown prince has come to kill Ahmad."
value.literal: Xi pressed the question; Yi then whispered in his ear: "The crown prince has come to execute Ahmad."

value.zh: 夜二鼓，忽聞人馬聲，遙見燭籠儀仗，將至宮門，其一人前呼啟關，觿謂九思曰：「他時殿下還宮，必以完澤、賽羊二人先，請得見二人，然後啟關。」
value.en: At the second watch he suddenly heard the sound of men and horses and saw candle lanterns and ceremonial escort approaching the palace gate. One man came forward calling for the gate to be opened. Xi told Jiusi, "When His Highness returns to the palace, Wanzhe and Saiyang always come first. Do not open the gate until you have seen them both."
value.literal: At the second watch of night suddenly the sound of men and horses was heard; from afar candle lanterns and ceremonial escort were seen approaching the palace gate; one man came forward calling to open the gate; Xi said to Jiusi: "When His Highness returns to the palace, Wanzhe and Saiyang must always come first—please see the two men, then open the gate."

value.zh: 觿呼二人不應，即語之曰：「皇太子平日未嘗行此門，今何來此也？」
value.en: Xi called for the two men, but there was no answer. He called out, "His Highness never uses this gate on ordinary days. Why come here now?"
value.literal: Xi called for the two men but there was no answer; he then said to them: "His Highness the crown prince on ordinary days has never used this gate—why come here now?"

value.zh: 賊計窮，趨南門。
value.en: Their stratagem exhausted, the rebels rushed for the south gate.
value.literal: The rebels' stratagem exhausted, they rushed for the south gate.

value.zh: 觿留張子政等守西門，亟走南門伺之。
value.en: Xi left Zhang Zizheng and others to guard the west gate and ran to the south gate to watch.
value.literal: Xi left Zhang Zizheng and others to guard the west gate and ran swiftly to the south gate to watch.

value.zh: 但聞傳呼省官姓名，燭影下遙見阿合馬及左丞郝禎已被殺。
value.en: He heard only the calling of Secretariat officials' names. In the candlelight he saw from afar that Ahmad and left vice councillor Hao Zhen had already been killed.
value.literal: He only heard the calling out of Secretariat officials' names; in the candlelight from afar he saw Ahmad and Left Vice Councillor Hao Zhen already killed.

value.zh: 觿乃與九思大呼曰：「此賊也！」
value.en: Xi and Jiusi shouted together, "These are rebels!"
value.literal: Xi then with Jiusi shouted loudly: "These are rebels!"

value.zh: 叱衛士急捕之，高和尚等皆潰去，惟王著就擒。
value.en: He ordered the guards to seize them at once. Gaoshanghe and the others scattered and fled; only Wang Zhu was captured.
value.literal: He ordered the guards to seize them swiftly; Gaoshanghe and others all scattered and fled, only Wang Zhu was captured.

value.zh: 黎明，中丞也先帖木兒與觿等馳驛往上都，以其事聞。
value.en: At dawn censor-in-chief Yesentiemur rode with Xi and others by relay to Shangdu to report what had happened.
value.literal: At dawn Censor-in-chief Yesentiemur with Xi and others galloped by relay to Shangdu to report the affair.

value.zh: 帝以中外未安，當益嚴武備，遂勞使遣亟還。
value.en: Because the realm was not yet settled within and without, the emperor said military readiness must be tightened further, comforted the envoys, and ordered them to return at once.
value.literal: The emperor, because within and without were not yet settled, should further tighten military readiness, therefore comforted the envoys and ordered them to return swiftly.

value.zh: 高和尚等尋皆伏誅。
value.en: Gaoshanghe and the others were soon all executed.
value.literal: Gaoshanghe and others soon all were executed after confession.

value.zh: 二十二年，遷嘉議大夫，同知大都留守司事，兼少府監。
value.en: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Grand Master of Advising Counsel, associate director of the Daidu garrison office, and concurrent director of the imperial household works.
value.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Grand Master of Advising Counsel, associate director of the Daidu garrison office, and concurrent director of the Imperial Household Works.

value.zh: 久之，遷中奉大夫、河南等路宣慰使。
value.en: After some time he was transferred to Grand Master of Correct Service and pacification commissioner of Henan and other circuits.
value.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Grand Master of Correct Service and pacification commissioner of Henan and other circuits.

value.zh: 卒，年五十三。
value.en: He died at the age of fifty-three.
value.literal: He died, age fifty-three.

value.zh: 張九思，字子有，燕宛平人。
value.en: Zhang Jiusi, whose style name was Ziyou, was a native of Wanping in the Yan region.
value.literal: Zhang Jiusi, styled Ziyou, was a native of Wanping in Yan.

value.zh: 父滋，薊州節度使。
value.en: His father Zi was military governor of Jizhou.
value.literal: His father Zi was military governor of Jizhou.

value.zh: 至元二年，九思入備宿衛，裕皇居東宮，一見奇之，以父廕當補外，特留不遣。
value.en: In the second year of the Zhiyuan era Jiusi entered the palace guard. Prince Yu, dwelling in the Eastern Palace, took an immediate liking to him. Though entitled by his father's privilege to an outside appointment, he was specially retained at court.
value.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan Jiusi entered to stand ready in the palace guard; Prince Yu dwelt in the Eastern Palace and at one sight found him remarkable; by his father's privilege he should have been assigned outside, but he was specially kept and not sent away.

value.zh: 江南既平，宋庫藏金帛輸內府，而分授東宮者多，置都總管府以主之，九思以工部尚書兼府事。
value.en: After Jiangnan was pacified, Song treasury gold and silks were delivered to the inner court, much of it allotted to the Eastern Palace. A chief steward's office was established to oversee these assets, and Jiusi served as minister of works with concurrent duties in that office.
value.literal: Once Jiangnan was pacified, Song treasury gold and silks were delivered to the inner court, but much was allotted to the Eastern Palace; a chief steward's office was established to oversee it, and Jiusi as Minister of Works concurrently held office affairs.

value.zh: 十九年春，世祖巡幸上都，皇太子從，丞相阿合馬留守。
value.en: In the spring of the nineteenth year Kublai progressed to Shangdu with the crown prince, while Chief Councillor Ahmad remained at Daidu.
value.literal: In spring of the nineteenth year the Founder made a progress to Shangdu, the crown prince followed, and Chief Councillor Ahmad remained on guard.

value.zh: 妖僧高和尚、千戶王著等謀殺之，夜聚數百人為儀衛，稱太子，入健德門，直趨東宮，傳令啟關甚遽。
value.en: The sorcerer-monk Gaoshanghe, chiliarch Wang Zhu, and others plotted his murder. By night they gathered several hundred men as a ceremonial guard, claimed to be the crown prince, entered Jiande Gate, and rushed straight to the Eastern Palace, urgently demanding that the gate be opened.
value.literal: The sorcerer-monk Gaoshanghe, chiliarch Wang Zhu, and others plotted to murder him; by night they gathered several hundred men as ceremonial guard, called themselves the crown prince, entered Jiande Gate, went straight to the Eastern Palace, and transmitted orders to open the gate with great urgency.

value.zh: 九思適直宿宮中，命主者不得擅啟關，語在《高觿傳》。
value.en: Jiusi happened to be on overnight guard in the palace and ordered the gatekeepers not to open the gate without authorization. The full account appears in the biography of Gao Xi.
value.literal: Jiusi happened to be on overnight guard in the palace and ordered the gatekeepers not to open the gate on their own authority—the account is in the biography of Gao Xi.

value.zh: 賊知不可紿，循垣趨南門外，擊殺丞相阿合馬、左丞郝禎。
value.en: Seeing they could not be deceived, the rebels followed the wall to the south gate, where they struck down Chief Councillor Ahmad and left vice councillor Hao Zhen.
value.literal: The rebels knew they could not be deceived, followed the wall to rush outside the south gate, and struck and killed Chief Councillor Ahmad and Left Vice Councillor Hao Zhen.

value.zh: 時變起倉卒，且昏夜，眾莫知所為，九思審其詐，叱宿衛士並力擊賊，盡獲之。
value.en: The disturbance broke out in haste on a dark night, and no one knew what to do. Jiusi saw through the deception, ordered the overnight guards to strike the rebels together, and captured them all.
value.literal: The disturbance arose in haste and it was also dark night; the crowd did not know what to do; Jiusi judged their deception and ordered the overnight guards to strike the rebels together with full force, capturing them all.

value.zh: 賊之入也，矯太子命，徵兵樞密副使張易，易不加審，遽以兵與之。
value.en: On entering, the rebels forged the crown prince's order to summon troops from privy council vice director Zhang Yi. Yi did not investigate and hastily gave them troops.
value.literal: When the rebels entered they forged the crown prince's order to summon troops from Privy Council Vice Director Zhang Yi; Yi did not examine it and hastily gave them troops.

value.zh: 易既坐誅，而刑官复論以知情，將傳首四方。
value.en: Yi was already executed, but the judicial officers argued that he had known of the plot and proposed sending his head to the four quarters as a warning.
value.literal: Yi was already condemned and executed, but the judicial officers again argued he had known and planned to transmit his head to the four quarters.

value.zh: 九思啟太子曰：「張易應變不審，而授賊以兵，死復何辭！
value.en: Jiusi reported to the crown prince, "Zhang Yi failed to judge the emergency and gave the rebels troops. Death is his only answer for that.
value.literal: Jiusi reported to the crown prince: "Zhang Yi did not examine the sudden change and gave the rebels troops—death leaves him nothing to say!

value.zh: 若坐以與謀，則過矣，請免傳首。」
value.en: But to convict him of joining the plot would be excessive. I beg that his head not be sent about the realm."
value.literal: If he is convicted of joining the plot, that is excessive—I beg to exempt transmitting his head."

value.zh: 皇太子言於帝，遂從之。
value.en: The crown prince spoke to the emperor, and the request was granted.
value.literal: The crown prince spoke to the emperor and it was followed.

value.zh: 九思討賊時，右衛指揮使顏進在行，中流矢卒，怨家誣為賊黨，將籍其孥，九思力辯之，得不坐。
value.en: During the suppression Right Guard commander Yan Jin was on the expedition, was struck by an arrow, and died. An enemy slandered him as a rebel accomplice and sought to punish his household. Jiusi argued forcefully on his behalf and the family was spared.
value.literal: When Jiusi suppressed the rebels, Right Guard Commander Yan Jin was on the expedition, was struck by an arrow and died; an enemy slandered him as a rebel accomplice and planned to register his household for punishment; Jiusi argued forcefully and he was not convicted.

value.zh: 周紀三
value.en: Zhou Records 3
value.literal: Zhou Records 3

value.zh: 張儀說魏襄王曰：「梁地方不至千里，卒不過三十萬，地四平，無名山大川之限，卒戍楚、韓、齊、趙之境，寧亭、障者不下十萬，梁之地勢固戰場也。
value.en: Zhang Yi urged King Xiang of Wei: "Liang's territory is under a thousand li, its soldiers under three hundred thousand; the land is flat on every side, with no great mountains or rivers to defend it; troops garrison the borders of Chu, Han, Qi, and Zhao; men in forts and barrier posts are not fewer than one hundred thousand; Liang's terrain is in truth a battlefield.
value.literal: Zhang Yi urged King Xiang of Wei, saying: "Liang's territory is less than a thousand li, its soldiers no more than three hundred thousand; the land is level on four sides, without famous mountains or great rivers to hem it in; soldiers garrison the borders of Chu, Han, Qi, and Zhao; those manning forts and barriers are not fewer than one hundred thousand; Liang's terrain is in truth a battlefield.

value.zh: 夫諸侯之約從，盟洹水之上，結為兄弟以相堅也。
value.en: When the lords ally vertically, they swear brotherhood above the Huan River to strengthen one another.
value.literal: When the feudal lords covenant in vertical alliance, they ally above the Huan River and bind themselves as brothers to strengthen one another.

value.zh: 今親兄弟同父母，尚有爭錢財相殺傷，而欲恃反覆蘇秦之餘謀，其不可成亦明矣。
value.en: Even full brothers of the same parents fight over money and wound one another—yet you would rely on the leftover schemes of the fickle Su Qin; that this cannot succeed is obvious.
value.literal: Now even full brothers of the same parents still fight over money and wound one another—yet you wish to rely on the leftover schemes of the fickle Su Qin; that it cannot succeed is clear.

value.zh: 大王不事秦，秦下兵攻河外，據卷衍、酸棗，劫衛，取陽晉，則趙不南，趙不南而梁不北，梁不北則從道絕，從道絕則大王之國欲毋危，不可得也。
value.en: If you do not serve Qin, Qin will march on Hewai, seize Juanyan and Suanzao, threaten Wei, and take Yangjin—Zhao cannot advance south; without Zhao in the south, Liang cannot advance north; without Liang in the north, the vertical alliance is severed; with that route cut, your state cannot hope to escape danger.
value.literal: If Your Majesty does not serve Qin, Qin will send troops down to attack Hewai, hold Juanyan and Suanzao, threaten Wei, and take Yangjin—then Zhao cannot go south; if Zhao cannot go south, Liang cannot go north; if Liang cannot go north, the vertical route is cut; if the vertical route is cut, then Your Majesty's state wishing not to be in peril—it cannot be obtained.

value.zh: 故願大王審定計議，且賜骸骨。」
value.en: So I beg Your Majesty to weigh your plans carefully and let me take my leave."
value.literal: Therefore I wish Your Majesty to examine and fix your plans, and grant me my bones."

value.zh: 魏王乃倍從約，而因儀以請成於秦。
value.en: King Xiang of Wei then broke the vertical alliance and, through Zhang Yi, sued for peace with Qin.
value.literal: The king of Wei thereupon doubled back on the vertical covenant and, through Yi, sought peace with Qin.

value.zh: 張儀歸，復相秦。
value.en: Zhang Yi returned and again became chancellor of Qin.
value.literal: Zhang Yi returned and again became chancellor of Qin.

value.zh: 巴、蜀相攻擊，俱告急於秦。
value.en: Ba and Shu attacked each other; both urgently appealed to Qin.
value.literal: Ba and Shu attacked each other; both urgently appealed to Qin.

value.zh: 秦惠王欲伐蜀。
value.en: King Hui of Qin wished to attack Shu.
value.literal: King Hui of Qin wished to attack Shu.

value.zh: 以為道險狹難至，而韓又來侵，猶豫未能決。
value.en: He thought the road perilous, narrow, and hard to reach, while Han raided again; he hesitated and could not decide.
value.literal: He thought the road perilous and narrow and hard to reach, while Han again came to raid; he hesitated and could not decide.

value.zh: 司馬錯請伐蜀。
value.en: Sima Cuo urged an attack on Shu.
value.literal: Sima Cuo requested to attack Shu.

value.zh: 張儀曰：「不如伐韓。」
value.en: Zhang Yi said: "Better to attack Han."
value.literal: Zhang Yi said: "Better to attack Han."

value.zh: 王曰：「請聞其說。」
value.en: The king said: "Let me hear your reasoning."
value.literal: The king said: "Please let me hear your reasoning."

value.zh: 儀曰：「親魏，善楚，下兵三川，攻新城、宜陽，以臨二周之郊，據九鼎，按圖籍，挾天子以令於天下，天下莫敢不聽，此王業也。
value.en: Zhang Yi said: "Befriend Wei, court Chu, march on the Three Rivers, attack Xincheng and Yiyang, threaten the Two Zhou, seize the Nine Cauldrons, hold the maps and registers, take the Son of Heaven hostage to command the realm—none under Heaven would dare disobey; that is true kingship.
value.literal: Yi said: "Be close to Wei, be good to Chu, send troops down to the Three Rivers, attack Xincheng and Yiyang, to overlook the suburbs of the Two Zhou, hold the Nine Cauldrons, consult maps and registers, seize the Son of Heaven to command the realm—none under Heaven dares not obey; this is kingship.

value.zh: 臣聞爭名者於朝，爭利者於市。
value.en: I have heard that men contend for fame at court and for profit in the market.
value.literal: Your servant has heard that those who contend for fame do so at court, and those who contend for profit do so in the market.

value.zh: 今三川、周室，天下之朝、市也，而王不爭焉，顧爭於戎翟，去王業遠矣！」
value.en: The Three Rivers and the Zhou court are the realm's court and market—yet you do not fight for them, but turn to fight barbarians; you are far from kingship!"
value.literal: Now the Three Rivers and the house of Zhou are the court and market of the realm—yet Your Majesty does not contend for them, but turns to contend with the Rong and Di; you are far from kingship!"

value.zh: 司馬錯曰：「不然，臣聞之，欲富國者務廣其地，欲強兵者務富其民，欲王者務博其德，三資者備而王隨之矣。
value.en: Sima Cuo said: "Not so. I have heard: to enrich the state, broaden its lands; to strengthen the army, enrich its people; to become king, spread your virtue—when these three are in place, kingship follows.
value.literal: Sima Cuo said: "Not so. Your servant has heard: one who wishes to enrich the state must broaden its territory; one who wishes to strengthen the army must enrich its people; one who wishes to be king must spread his virtue—when these three resources are complete, kingship follows.

value.zh: 今王地小民貧，故臣願先從事於易。
value.en: Your territory is small and your people poor; so I wish to begin with what is easy.
value.literal: Now Your Majesty's territory is small and the people poor; therefore your servant wishes first to undertake what is easy.

value.zh: 夫蜀，西僻之國而戎翟之長也，有桀、紂之亂，以秦攻之，譬如使豺狼逐群羊。
value.en: Shu is a remote western state, chief among the barbarians; it has chaos like that of Jie and Zhou—if Qin attacks it, it is like setting wolves on a flock of sheep.
value.literal: Shu is a remote western state and chief among the Rong and Di; it has the disorder of Jie and Zhou—if Qin attacks it, it is like setting wolves and jackals on a flock of sheep.

value.zh: 得其地足以廣國，取其財足以富民，繕兵不傷眾而彼已服焉。
value.en: Its land would widen your realm, its wealth would enrich your people; you could ready your army without heavy losses, and they would already submit.
value.literal: Gaining its land suffices to broaden the state; taking its wealth suffices to enrich the people; drilling troops without harming the masses, and they already submit.

value.zh: 拔一國而天下不以為暴，利盡西海而天下不以為貪，是我一舉而名實附也，而又有禁暴止亂之名。
value.en: You would overthrow one state yet the realm would not call you violent; profits reaching the western seas yet the realm would not call you greedy—in one stroke we gain both fame and substance, and the name of ending violence and chaos.
value.literal: Uprooting one state yet the realm does not deem you violent; profits extending to the western seas yet the realm does not deem you greedy—thus in one move fame and substance attach to us, and we also have the name of forbidding violence and stopping disorder.

value.zh: 今攻韓，劫天子，惡名也，而未必利也，又有不義之名，而攻天下所不欲，危矣！
value.en: To attack Han now, seize the Son of Heaven—that wins an evil name without sure profit, adds the name of injustice, and strikes where the realm does not wish—perilous!
value.literal: Now to attack Han, seize the Son of Heaven—an evil name, and not necessarily profit; moreover an unrighteous name, attacking what the realm does not wish—perilous!

value.zh: 臣請論其故。
value.en: Let me explain why.
value.literal: Your servant requests to discuss the reasons.

value.zh: 周，天下之宗室也；
value.en: Zhou is the ancestral house of the realm;
value.literal: Zhou is the ancestral house of the realm;

value.zh: 齊，韓之與國也。
value.en: Qi is Han's ally.
value.literal: Qi is Han's allied state.

value.zh: 周自知失九鼎，韓自知亡三川，將二國並力合謀，以因乎齊、趙而求解乎楚、魏。
value.en: Zhou knows it has lost the Nine Cauldrons; Han knows it has lost the Three Rivers; the two will join forces, lean on Qi and Zhao, and seek aid from Chu and Wei.
value.literal: Zhou itself knows it has lost the Nine Cauldrons; Han itself knows it has lost the Three Rivers; the two states will combine strength and join plots, rely on Qi and Zhao, and seek rescue from Chu and Wei.

value.zh: 以鼎與楚，以地與魏，王弗能止也。
value.en: They will give the cauldrons to Chu and land to Wei—and you cannot stop it.
value.literal: They will give the cauldrons to Chu and the lands to Wei—Your Majesty cannot stop it.

value.zh: 此臣之所謂危也。
value.en: That is what I call peril.
value.literal: This is what your servant calls peril.

value.zh: 不如伐蜀完。」
value.en: Better to finish the conquest of Shu."
value.literal: Better to attack Shu to completion."

value.zh: 王從錯計，起兵伐蜀。
value.en: The king followed Sima Cuo's plan and marched on Shu.
value.literal: The king followed Cuo's plan and raised troops to attack Shu.

value.zh: 十月取之。
value.en: In the tenth month he conquered it.
value.literal: In the tenth month he took it.

value.zh: 貶蜀王，更號為侯，而使陳莊相蜀。
value.en: He demoted the Shu king to marquis and sent Chen Zhuang to govern Shu.
value.literal: He demoted the king of Shu, changed his title to marquis, and sent Chen Zhuang to govern Shu.

value.zh: 蜀既屬秦，秦以益強，富厚，輕諸侯。
value.en: Once Shu belonged to Qin, Qin grew stronger and richer and held the feudal lords in contempt.
value.literal: Once Shu belonged to Qin, Qin thereby grew stronger, rich and substantial, and looked lightly on the feudal lords.

value.zh: 秦王欲伐齊，患齊、楚之從親，乃使張儀至楚，說楚王曰：「大王誠能聽臣，閉關絕約於齊，臣請獻商於之地六百里，使秦女得為大王箕帚之妾，秦、楚娶婦嫁女，長為兄弟之國。」
value.en: The king of Qin planned to attack Qi but feared the Qi–Chu alliance, so he sent Zhang Yi to Chu. Zhang Yi told the king: “If Your Majesty will heed me, close the passes and break with Qi—I will give you six hundred li in Shangyu, provide a Qin bride to serve in your household, and bind Qin and Chu in marriage so we remain brother states forever.”
value.literal: The king of Qin wished to attack Qi and worried over the horizontal alliance of Qi and Chu; he therefore sent Zhang Yi to Chu to persuade the king of Chu, saying: “If Your Majesty will truly heed me, close the passes and break the treaty with Qi—I beg to present six hundred li of Shangyu land, let a Qin girl become Your Majesty’s wife who sweeps and serves, and Qin and Chu marry daughters and take wives, to be brother states forever.”

value.zh: 楚王說而許之。
value.en: The king of Chu was delighted and agreed.
value.literal: The king of Chu was pleased and assented.

value.zh: 君臣皆賀，陳軫獨吊。
value.en: Court and king rejoiced; only Chen Zhen mourned.
value.literal: Ministers and ruler all congratulated him; Chen Zhen alone offered condolences.

value.zh: 王怒曰：「寡人不興師而得六百里地，何吊也？」
value.en: The king said angrily: “I gain six hundred li without raising troops—why mourn?”
value.literal: The king said angrily: “Without raising troops I gain six hundred li of land—why offer condolences?”

value.zh: 對曰：「不然。
value.en: He replied: “Not so.
value.literal: He replied: “It is not so.

value.zh: 以臣觀之，商於之地不可得而齊、秦合。
value.en: In my view you will not get Shangyu, and Qi and Qin will join.
value.literal: In your servant’s view, the land of Shangyu cannot be obtained, and Qi and Qin will unite.

value.zh: 齊、秦合則患必至矣！」
value.en: When Qi and Qin unite, disaster is certain!”
value.literal: When Qi and Qin unite, calamity is sure to come!”

value.zh: 王曰：「有說乎？」
value.en: The king said: “Explain.”
value.literal: The king said: “Have you an explanation?”

value.zh: 對曰：「夫秦之所以重楚者，以其有齊也。
value.en: He said: “Qin values Chu because you have Qi as ally.
value.literal: He replied: “Qin values Chu because Chu has Qi.

value.zh: 今閉關絕約於齊，則楚孤，秦奚貪夫孤國，而與之商於之地六百里？
value.en: Close the passes and break with Qi, and Chu stands alone—why should Qin favor a lonely state with six hundred li of Shangyu?
value.literal: Now if you close the passes and break the treaty with Qi, Chu is isolated—why should Qin covet such an isolated state as to give it six hundred li of Shangyu?

value.zh: 張儀至秦，必負王。
value.en: When Zhang Yi returns to Qin he will surely betray you.
value.literal: When Zhang Yi reaches Qin, he is sure to betray Your Majesty.

value.zh: 是王北絕齊交，西生患於秦也。
value.en: You will cut off Qi in the north and breed trouble with Qin in the west.
value.literal: Thus Your Majesty will cut off Qi in the north and breed trouble with Qin in the west.

value.zh: 兩國之兵必俱至。
value.en: Armies from both states will surely come against you.
value.literal: The armies of both states are sure to come together.

value.zh: 為王計者，不若陰合而陽絕於齊，使人隨張儀。
value.en: Better secretly stay aligned with Qi while openly breaking off, and send someone to follow Zhang Yi.
value.literal: For Your Majesty’s planning, it would be better to unite with Qi in secret while openly breaking with them, and send someone to follow Zhang Yi.

value.zh: 苟與吾地，絕齊未晚也。」
value.en: If he gives the land, breaking with Qi will not be too late.”
value.literal: If he truly gives us the land, breaking with Qi is not yet late.”

value.zh: 王曰「願陳子閉口，毋復言，以待寡人得地！」
value.en: The king said, “Counselor Chen, be silent until I have the land!”
value.literal: The king said, “I wish Counselor Chen would close his mouth and speak no more, until I have gained the land!”

value.zh: 乃以相印授張儀，厚賜之。
value.en: He gave Zhang Yi the chancellor’s seal and rich gifts.
value.literal: He thereupon gave Zhang Yi the seal of chancellor and richly rewarded him.

value.zh: 遂閉關絕約於齊，使一將軍隨張儀至秦。
value.en: He closed the passes, broke with Qi, and sent a general to accompany Zhang Yi to Qin.
value.literal: He then closed the passes and broke the treaty with Qi, and sent a general to follow Zhang Yi to Qin.

value.zh: 張儀佯墮車，不朝三月。
value.en: Zhang Yi pretended to fall from his carriage and stayed away from court for three months.
value.literal: Zhang Yi pretended to fall from his carriage and did not attend court for three months.

value.zh: 楚王聞之，曰：「儀以寡人絕齊未甚邪？」
value.en: The king of Chu heard this and said: “Does Zhang Yi think I have not broken with Qi thoroughly enough?”
value.literal: The king of Chu heard of it and said: “Has Yi thought my break with Qi not thorough enough?”

value.zh: 乃使勇士宋遺借宋之符，北罵齊王。
value.en: He sent the warrior Song Yi, using Song’s credentials, north to insult the king of Qi.
value.literal: He thereupon sent the warrior Song Yi, borrowing Song’s tally, to go north and revile the king of Qi.

value.zh: 齊王大怒，折節而事秦，齊、秦之交合。
value.en: The king of Qi was furious, humbled himself to court Qin, and Qi and Qin allied.
value.literal: The king of Qi was greatly enraged, bent his dignity to serve Qin, and Qi and Qin’s alliance was joined.

value.zh: 張儀乃朝，見楚使者曰：「子何不受地？
value.en: Zhang Yi then appeared at court and asked the Chu envoy: “Why do you not take your land?
value.literal: Zhang Yi then attended court and, seeing the Chu envoy, said: “Why do you not receive the land?

value.zh: 從某至某，廣袤六里。」
value.en: From here to here—six li square.”
value.literal: From such-and-such a place to such-and-such a place—six li in length and breadth.”

value.zh: 使者怒，還報楚王。
value.en: The envoy was furious and returned to report to the king of Chu.
value.literal: The envoy was enraged and returned to report to the king of Chu.

value.zh: 楚王大怒，欲發兵而攻秦。
value.en: The king of Chu was furious and wanted to march against Qin.
value.literal: The king of Chu was greatly enraged and wished to raise troops to attack Qin.

value.zh: 陳軫曰：「軫可發口言乎？
value.en: Chen Zhen said: “May I speak?
value.literal: Chen Zhen said: “May Zhen open his mouth to speak?

value.zh: 攻之不如因賂以一名都，與之并兵而攻齊，是我亡地於秦，取償於齊也。
value.en: Better than attacking: offer a great city in tribute and join forces to attack Qi—thus we lose land to Qin but gain compensation from Qi.
value.literal: To attack is not as good as bribing them with a famous city and joining with them in troops to attack Qi—thus we lose land to Qin but take compensation from Qi.

value.zh: 今王已絕於齊而責欺於秦，是吾合秦、齊之交而來天下之兵也，國必大傷矣！」
value.en: You have already broken with Qi yet blame Qin for deceit—you unite Qin and Qi and invite every army under Heaven; the state will be gravely wounded!”
value.literal: Now Your Majesty has broken with Qi yet holds Qin to account for deceit—this joins the alliances of Qin and Qi and brings the armies of the realm; the state is sure to suffer great harm!”

value.zh: 楚王不聽，使屈匄帥師伐秦。
value.en: The king would not listen and sent Qu Gai to command the attack on Qin.
value.literal: The king of Chu would not heed him and sent Qu Gai to lead the army against Qin.

value.zh: 秦亦發兵使庶長章擊之。
value.en: Qin also mobilized and sent Chief Assistant Zhang against him.
value.literal: Qin also raised troops and sent Chief Assistant Zhang to strike him.

value.zh: 秦惠王使人告楚懷王，請以武關之外易黔中地。
value.en: King Hui of Qin sent an envoy to King Huai of Chu, offering to trade the territory beyond Wu Pass for Qianzhong.
value.literal: King Hui of Qin sent someone to inform King Huai of Chu, proposing to exchange the lands outside Wu Pass for Qianzhong.

value.zh: 楚王曰：「不願易地，願得張儀而獻黔中地。」
value.en: The king of Chu said, “I do not want a land swap. Give me Zhang Yi and I will yield Qianzhong.”
value.literal: The king of Chu said, “I do not wish to exchange lands; I wish to have Zhang Yi and will offer Qianzhong.”

value.zh: 張儀聞之，請行。
value.en: Zhang Yi heard and asked leave to go.
value.literal: Zhang Yi heard this and asked to go.

value.zh: 王曰：「楚將甘心於子，奈何行？」
value.en: The king said, “Chu will have your life—how can you go?”
value.literal: The king said, “Chu will eagerly devour you—how can you go?”

value.zh: 張儀曰：「秦強楚弱，大王在，楚不宜敢取臣。
value.en: Zhang Yi said, “Qin is strong and Chu weak. While Your Majesty lives, Chu will not dare touch me.
value.literal: Zhang Yi said, “Qin is strong and Chu weak; while Your Majesty lives, Chu ought not dare take me.

value.zh: 且臣善其嬖臣靳尚，靳尚得事幸姬鄭袖，袖之言，王無不聽者。」
value.en: Besides, I am close to his favorite Jin Shang, who serves the favored consort Zheng Xiu. Whatever she says, the king hears.”
value.literal: Moreover I am on good terms with his favorite Jin Shang; Jin Shang waits on the favored consort Zheng Xiu, and whatever Xiu says the king never fails to heed.”

value.zh: 遂往。
value.en: And he went.
value.literal: Thereupon he went.

value.zh: 楚王囚，將殺之。
value.en: The king of Chu seized him and meant to kill him.
value.literal: The king of Chu imprisoned him and was about to kill him.

value.zh: 靳尚謂鄭袖曰：「秦王甚愛張儀，將以上庸六縣及美女贖之。
value.en: Jin Shang told Zheng Xiu, “The king of Qin loves Zhang Yi and will ransom him with the six counties of Shangyong and fair women.
value.literal: Jin Shang said to Zheng Xiu, “The king of Qin loves Zhang Yi dearly and will ransom him with the six counties of Shangyong and beautiful women.

value.zh: 王重地尊秦，秦女必貴而夫人斥矣。」
value.en: The king prizes land and defers to Qin. A Qin woman will rise high, and my lady will be cast aside.”
value.literal: The king values territory and honors Qin; a woman of Qin will surely be exalted and my lady driven aside.”

value.zh: 於是鄭袖日夜泣於楚王曰：「臣各為其主耳。
value.en: Zheng Xiu wept before the king day and night: “Every minister serves his own lord.
value.literal: Thereupon Zheng Xiu wept day and night before the king of Chu, saying, “Ministers each serve their own lord.

value.zh: 今殺張儀，秦必大怒。
value.en: Kill Zhang Yi now and Qin will rage.
value.literal: Kill Zhang Yi now and Qin will surely rage.

value.zh: 妾請子母俱遷江南，毋為秦所魚肉也！」
value.en: Let me take our son and move south of the Yangtze, lest Qin cut us like fish on a board!”
value.literal: I beg that you and I, mother and son, move together to the lands south of the Yangtze, lest we be carved up like fish on Qin’s board!”

value.zh: 王乃赦張儀而厚禮之。
value.en: The king pardoned Zhang Yi and treated him with great honor.
value.literal: The king then pardoned Zhang Yi and entertained him generously.

value.zh: 張儀因說楚王曰：「夫為從者無以異於驅群羊而攻猛虎，不格明矣。
value.en: Zhang Yi then urged the king of Chu: “A horizontal alliance is no different from driving sheep against a tiger. The folly is plain.
value.literal: Zhang Yi then persuaded the king of Chu, saying, “For those in a horizontal alliance there is no difference from driving a flock of sheep to attack a fierce tiger—the inaptness is clear.

value.zh: 今王不事秦，秦劫韓驅梁而攻楚，則楚危矣。
value.en: If Your Majesty will not serve Qin, Qin will seize Han, drive Liang, and strike Chu—and Chu will be lost.
value.literal: Now if Your Majesty does not serve Qin, Qin will seize Han and drive Liang to attack Chu—then Chu will be in peril.

value.zh: 秦西有巴、蜀，治船積粟，浮岷江而下，一日行五百餘里，不至十日而拒扞關，扞關驚則從境以東盡城守矣，黔中、巫郡非王之有。
value.en: West of Qin lie Ba and Shu. They build ships and hoard grain, float down the Min—five hundred li a day. In ten days they reach Hanguan. When Hanguan stirs, every city east of the border will shut its gates. Qianzhong and Wujun will no longer be yours.
value.literal: Qin has Ba and Shu in the west; it builds boats and stocks grain, floats down the Min River—more than five hundred li in a day; in less than ten days it reaches Hanguan; when Hanguan is alarmed, from the border east all will garrison the cities—Qianzhong and Wujun will no longer be yours.

value.zh: 秦舉甲出武關，則北地絕。
value.en: Qin marches from Wu Pass and your northern lands are severed.
value.literal: Qin raises armor and issues from Wu Pass, and the northern lands are cut off.

value.zh: 秦兵之攻楚也，危難在三月之內，而楚待諸侯之救在半歲之外。
value.en: Qin can bring Chu to ruin in three months, while Chu must wait half a year for the lords’ aid.
value.literal: When Qin troops attack Chu, peril comes within three months, yet Chu waits for rescue from the feudal lords beyond half a year.

value.zh: 夫待弱國之救，忘強秦之禍，此臣所為大王患也。
value.en: To wait on weak allies and forget the threat of mighty Qin—that is what I fear for Your Majesty.
value.literal: To await rescue from weak states while forgetting calamity from mighty Qin—this is what your servant fears for Your Majesty.

value.zh: 大王誠能聽臣，臣請令秦、楚長為兄弟之國，無相攻伐。」
value.en: If Your Majesty will hear me, I beg to make Qin and Chu brother states forever, never to attack each other.”
value.literal: If Your Majesty will truly hear me, your servant begs to make Qin and Chu brother states forever, never attacking each other.”

value.zh: 楚王已得張儀而重出黔中地，乃許之。
value.en: The king of Chu, having Zhang Yi, still tried to keep Qianzhong, but at last agreed.
value.literal: The king of Chu, having Zhang Yi in hand, still wished to withhold Qianzhong, yet in the end agreed.

value.zh: 張儀遂之韓，說韓王曰：「韓地險惡山居，五穀所生，非菽而麥，國無二歲之食，見卒不過二十萬。
value.en: Zhang Yi went on to Han and told the king: “Han is rugged and mountainous. Its fields yield little but beans and wheat. The state has less than two years’ grain. Its troops number at most two hundred thousand.
value.literal: Zhang Yi then went to Han and said to the king of Han, “Han’s lands are rugged and mountainous; of the grains they grow, none is not bean or wheat; the state has not two years’ food; visible troops number no more than two hundred thousand.

value.zh: 秦被甲百餘萬。
value.en: Qin fields more than a million armored men.
value.literal: Qin has more than a million in armor.

value.zh: 山東之士被甲蒙冑而會戰，秦人捐甲徒裼以趨敵，左挈人頭，右挾生虜。
value.en: The lords east of the mountains arm and helm for battle; Qin’s men cast off mail and rush in bare skin, a head in the left hand, a captive in the right.
value.literal: The warriors east of the mountains don armor and helms to meet in battle; the men of Qin cast off armor and rush bare to the foe, seizing heads in the left hand and living captives in the right.

value.zh: 夫戰孟賁、烏獲之士以攻不服之弱國，無異垂千鈞之重於鳥卵之上，必無幸矣。
value.en: To pit men like Meng Bo and Wu Huo against a weak state that will not yield is to hang a thousand jun on a bird’s egg—there is no hope.
value.literal: To fight with men like Meng Bo and Wu Huo against a weak state that will not submit is no different from hanging a weight of a thousand jun on a bird’s egg—there can be no escape.

value.zh: 大王不事秦，秦下甲據宜陽，塞成皋，則王之國分矣。
value.en: If Your Majesty will not serve Qin, Qin will march down, seize Yiyang, and choke Chenggao—and your realm will be cut in two.
value.literal: If Your Majesty does not serve Qin, Qin will descend with armor, hold Yiyang, block Chenggao—and Your Majesty’s state will be split.

value.zh: 鴻臺之宮，桑林之宛，非王之有也。
value.en: The palace at Hongtai, the park at Sanglin—they will no longer be yours.
value.literal: The palace of Hongtai, the parklands of Sanglin—will no longer be yours.

value.zh: 為大王計，莫如事秦而攻楚，以轉禍而悅秦，計無便於此者。」
value.en: For Your Majesty, nothing is wiser than to serve Qin and strike Chu—turn disaster to gain, please Qin. No plan is better.”
value.literal: For Your Majesty’s counsel, nothing surpasses serving Qin and attacking Chu, turning calamity to favor with Qin—no plan is more expedient.”

value.zh: 韓王許之。
value.en: The king of Han agreed.
value.literal: The king of Han agreed.

value.zh: 張儀歸報，秦王封以六邑，號武信君。
value.en: Zhang Yi returned and reported. The king of Qin gave him six towns and the title Lord Martial Faith.
value.literal: Zhang Yi returned to report; the king of Qin enfeoffed him with six towns and titled him Lord Martial Faith.

value.zh: 復使東說齊王曰：「從人說大王者必曰：『齊蔽於三晉，地廣民眾，兵強士勇，雖有百秦，將無奈齊何。』
value.en: "He was sent east again to the king of Qi: The alliance men will tell Your Majesty, Qi is shielded by the Three Jin. Your lands are broad, your people many, your arms strong, your warriors brave. Even a hundred Qins cannot touch Qi.
value.literal: "He was again sent east to persuade the king of Qi, saying, Those of the horizontal alliance who speak to Your Majesty will surely say, Qi is screened by the Three Jin; its lands are broad, its people many; its arms strong, its warriors brave—even a hundred Qins can do nothing to Qi.

value.zh: 大王賢其說而不計其實。
value.en: Your Majesty admires the words and ignores the fact.
value.literal: Your Majesty admires their words and does not reckon the reality.

value.zh: 今秦、楚嫁女娶婦，為昆弟之國；
value.en: Now Qin and Chu exchange brides and are brother states;
value.literal: Now Qin and Chu marry daughters and take wives, becoming brother states;

value.zh: 韓獻宜陽；
value.en: Han has yielded Yiyang;
value.literal: Han has offered Yiyang;

value.zh: 梁效河外；
value.en: Liang has surrendered the lands beyond the River;
value.literal: Liang has presented the lands beyond the River;

value.zh: 趙王入朝，割河間以事秦。
value.en: the king of Zhao has come to court and ceded Hejian to serve Qin.
value.literal: the king of Zhao has come to court and ceded Hejian to serve Qin.

value.zh: 大王不事秦，秦驅韓、梁攻齊之南地，悉趙兵，渡清河，指博關，臨菑、即墨非王之有也！
value.en: If Your Majesty will not serve Qin, Qin will drive Han and Liang against Qi’s south, muster Zhao, cross the Clear River, take Bomen—Linzi and Jimo will no longer be yours!
value.literal: If Your Majesty does not serve Qin, Qin will drive Han and Liang to attack Qi’s southern lands, muster Zhao’s troops, cross the Clear River, point at Bomen—Linzi and Jimo will no longer be yours!

value.zh: 國一日見攻，雖欲事秦，不可得也！」
value.en: Once your state is struck, you may wish to serve Qin—but it will be too late!”
value.literal: Once the state is attacked in a day, even if you wish to serve Qin, it cannot be done!”

value.zh: 齊王許張儀。
value.en: The king of Qi agreed.
value.literal: The king of Qi agreed to Zhang Yi.

value.zh: 張儀去，西說趙王曰：「大王收率天下以擯秦，秦兵不敢出函谷關十五年。
value.en: Zhang Yi went west to the king of Zhao: “Your Majesty rallied the world against Qin. For fifteen years Qin’s armies did not pass Hangu Pass.
value.literal: Zhang Yi departed and went west to persuade the king of Zhao, saying, “Your Majesty gathered and led the world to shut out Qin; Qin’s troops dared not leave Hangu Pass for fifteen years.

value.zh: 大王之威行於山東，敝邑恐懼，繕甲厲兵，力田積粟，愁居懾處，不敢動搖，唯大王有意督過之也。
value.en: Your Majesty’s power filled the east. Our poor state feared, repaired arms, tilled fields, hoarded grain, lived in dread, and dared not move—only hoping Your Majesty might yet reprove us.
value.literal: Your Majesty’s might ran through the lands east of the mountains; our humble state feared, repaired armor and sharpened weapons, labored in the fields and stored grain, dwelt in worry and dread, dared not stir—only that Your Majesty might deign to reprove us.

value.zh: 今以大王之力，舉巴、蜀，並漢中，包兩周，守白馬之津。
value.en: Now, by Your Majesty’s power, we have taken Ba and Shu, joined Hanzhong, enclosed the Two Zhou, and hold the ford of White Horse.
value.literal: Now by Your Majesty’s strength Qin has taken Ba and Shu, annexed Hanzhong, wrapped the Two Zhou, and holds the ford of White Horse.

value.zh: 秦雖僻遠，然而心忿含怒之日久矣。
value.en: Qin is far away, yet our hearts have nursed wrath a long time.
value.literal: Though Qin is remote, hearts have long heaped wrath and held rage.

value.zh: 今秦有敝甲凋兵軍於澠池，願渡河，逾漳，據番吾，會邯鄲之下，願以甲子合戰，正殷紂之事。
value.en: Now we have battered armor and weary troops at Mianchi. We mean to cross the River, pass Zhang, hold Fanwu, and meet you below Handan. We ask battle on jiazi day—to settle what King Zhou of Yin left undone.
value.literal: Now Qin has worn armor and withered troops encamped at Mianchi; we wish to cross the River, pass Zhang, hold Fanwu, meet below Handan—we wish to join battle on jiazi and set right the affair of King Zhou of Yin.

value.zh: 謹使使臣先聞左右。
value.en: I send this envoy first to inform Your Majesty.
value.literal: I respectfully send an envoy first to inform those at your side.

value.zh: 今楚與秦為昆弟之國，而韓、梁稱東籓之臣，齊獻魚鹽之地，此斷趙之右肩也。
value.en: Chu and Qin are brothers. Han and Liang are your eastern vassals. Qi has yielded its coast. This cuts off Zhao’s right arm.
value.literal: Now Chu and Qin are brother states, while Han and Liang call themselves eastern vassals and Qi has offered its fish-and-salt lands—this severs Zhao’s right shoulder.

value.zh: 夫斷右肩而與人鬥，失其黨而孤居，求欲毋危，得乎？
value.en: Cut off your right arm and fight—lose your allies and stand alone. Can you hope to be safe?
value.literal: Sever the right shoulder and fight another—lose your party and stand alone; can you seek not to be imperiled and succeed?

value.zh: 今秦發三將軍，其一軍塞午道，告齊使渡清河，軍於邯鄲之東；
value.en: Qin now sends three generals. One blocks Wudao and tells Qi to cross the Clear River and camp east of Handan;
value.literal: Now Qin sends three generals: one army blocks Wudao, tells Qi to cross the Clear River and encamp east of Handan;

value.zh: 一軍軍成皋，驅韓、梁軍於河外；
value.en: one camps at Chenggao and drives Han and Liang beyond the River;
value.literal: one army encamps at Chenggao and drives Han and Liang’s troops beyond the River;

value.zh: 一軍軍於澠池，約四國為一以攻趙，趙服必四分其地。
value.en: one camps at Mianchi and binds four states to strike Zhao. When Zhao yields, its land will be carved four ways.
value.literal: one army encamps at Mianchi, binds four states as one to attack Zhao—when Zhao submits, its lands will surely be quartered.

value.zh: 臣竊為大王計，莫如與秦王面相約而口相結，常為兄弟之國也。」
value.en: I urge Your Majesty: meet the king of Qin face to face, swear brotherhood, and stand as brothers forever.”
value.literal: Your servant privately counsels Your Majesty: nothing surpasses meeting the king of Qin face to face, binding with spoken oath, ever to be brother states.”

value.zh: 趙王許之。
value.en: The king of Zhao agreed.
value.literal: The king of Zhao agreed.

value.zh: 張儀乃北之燕，說燕王曰：「今趙王已入朝，效河間以事秦。
value.en: Zhang Yi went north to Yan and told the king: “The king of Zhao has come to court and yielded Hejian to serve Qin.
value.literal: Zhang Yi then went north to Yan and said to the king of Yan, “Now the king of Zhao has come to court and offered Hejian to serve Qin.

value.zh: 大王不事秦，秦下甲雲中、九原，驅趙而攻燕，則易水、長城非大王之有也。
value.en: If Your Majesty will not serve Qin, Qin will march through Yunzhong and Jiuyuan, drive Zhao against Yan—and the Yi River and the Long Wall will no longer be yours.
value.literal: If Your Majesty does not serve Qin, Qin will descend with armor through Yunzhong and Jiuyuan, drive Zhao to attack Yan—then the Yi River and the Long Wall will no longer be yours.

value.zh: 且今時齊、趙之於秦，猶郡縣也，不敢妄舉師以攻伐。
value.en: Qi and Zhao toward Qin are now like commanderies. They dare not raise armies against you.
value.literal: Moreover, Qi and Zhao toward Qin now are like commanderies and counties—they dare not rashly raise armies to attack.

value.zh: 今王事秦，長無齊、趙之患矣。」
value.en: Serve Qin, and you will be free of Qi and Zhao forever.”
value.literal: If Your Majesty serves Qin now, you will long be free of trouble from Qi and Zhao.”

value.zh: 燕王請獻常山之尾五城以和。
value.en: The king of Yan offered five towns at the foot of Mount Chang to make peace.
value.literal: The king of Yan asked to offer the five towns at the tail of Mount Chang to make peace.

value.zh: 張儀歸報，未至咸陽，秦惠王薨，子武王立。
value.en: Zhang Yi turned homeward to report. Before he reached Xianyang, King Hui of Qin died and his son King Wu succeeded.
value.literal: Zhang Yi returned to report; before he reached Xianyang, King Hui of Qin died and his son King Wu succeeded.

value.zh: 武王自為太子時，不悅張儀，及即位，群臣多毀短之。
value.en: As crown prince, King Wu had disliked Zhang Yi. When he took the throne, many ministers slandered him.
value.literal: King Wu, from the time he was heir, disliked Zhang Yi; when he took the throne, many among the ministers slandered him.

value.zh: 諸侯聞儀與秦王有隙，皆畔衡，復合從。
value.en: The lords heard that Yi and Qin were estranged. All left the vertical alliance and joined the horizontal again.
value.literal: The feudal lords heard that Yi and the king of Qin were at odds; all turned from the vertical alliance and joined the horizontal again.

value.zh: 張儀說秦武王曰：「為王計者，東方有變，然後王可以多割得地也。
value.en: Zhang Yi told King Wu of Qin: “For Your Majesty’s sake, when the east is in turmoil, you may win more land.
value.literal: Zhang Yi said to King Wu of Qin, “For Your Majesty’s plan, when there is change in the east, then Your Majesty may take more land in cession.

value.zh: 臣聞齊王甚憎臣，臣之所在，齊必伐之。
value.en: I hear the king of Qi hates me. Wherever I am, Qi will attack.
value.literal: I hear the king of Qi hates me deeply; wherever I am, Qi will surely attack.

value.zh: 臣願乞其不肖之身以之梁，齊必伐梁，齊、梁交兵而不能相去，王以其間伐韓，入三川，挾天子，案圖籍，此王業也。」
value.en: Let me take my worthless self to Liang. Qi will strike Liang. While Qi and Liang fight and cannot break off, Your Majesty may attack Han, enter the Three Rivers, hold the Son of Heaven, and read the maps and registers—that is the royal enterprise.”
value.literal: I beg to offer my unworthy person to Liang; Qi will surely attack Liang. When Qi and Liang fight and cannot break away, Your Majesty may use the interval to attack Han, enter the Three Rivers, hold the Son of Heaven, examine maps and registers—this is the royal enterprise.”

value.zh: 王許之。
value.en: The king agreed.
value.literal: The king agreed.

value.zh: 齊王果伐梁，梁王恐。
value.en: Qi did attack Liang, and the king of Liang was afraid.
value.literal: The king of Qi did attack Liang; the king of Liang was afraid.

value.zh: 張儀曰：「王勿患也。
value.en: Zhang Yi said, “Do not fear.
value.literal: Zhang Yi said, “Your Majesty, do not worry.

value.zh: 請令齊罷兵。」
value.en: I will make Qi withdraw.”
value.literal: I beg to make Qi cease its troops.”

value.zh: 乃使其舍人之楚，借使謂齊王曰：「甚矣，王之托儀於秦也！」
value.en: He sent a retainer to Chu, borrowed an envoy, and told the king of Qi: “How deeply Your Majesty has trusted Yi to Qin!”
value.literal: He then sent his retainer to Chu, borrowing an envoy to say to the king of Qi, “How far Your Majesty has entrusted Yi to Qin!”

value.zh: 齊王曰：「何故？」
value.en: The king of Qi asked, “Why?”
value.literal: The king of Qi said, “Why?”

value.zh: 楚使者曰：「張儀之去秦也，固與秦王謀矣，欲齊、梁相攻而令秦取三川也。
value.en: The Chu envoy said, “When Zhang Yi left Qin he plotted with the king: he meant Qi and Liang to fight so Qin could take the Three Rivers.
value.literal: The Chu envoy said, “When Zhang Yi left Qin he had surely plotted with the king of Qin: he wished Qi and Liang to fight each other so that Qin might take the Three Rivers.

value.zh: 今王果伐梁，是王內罷國而外伐與國，以信儀於秦王也。」
value.en: Now you have attacked Liang—you wear out your state within, strike an ally without, and prove Yi true to the king of Qin.”
value.literal: Now Your Majesty has indeed attacked Liang—this is to exhaust your state within while attacking an allied state without, and to give credence to Yi before the king of Qin.”

value.zh: 齊王乃解兵還。
value.en: Qi withdrew its army.
value.literal: The king of Qi then dismissed his troops and returned.

value.zh: 張儀相魏一歲，夏，五月，儀卒。
value.en: Zhang Yi served as chancellor of Wei one year; in summer, fifth month, Yi died.
value.literal: Zhang Yi was chancellor of Wei one year; in summer, fifth month, Yi died.

value.zh: 儀與蘇秦皆以縱橫之術游諸侯，致位富貴，天下爭慕效之。
value.en: Yi and Su Qin both won rank and riches by the arts of alliance and defiance among the lords; the world rushed to imitate them.
value.literal: Yi and Su Qin both roamed the feudal lords with the arts of vertical and horizontal alliance, reaching rank and wealth; the world vied to admire and imitate them.

value.zh: 又有魏人公孫衍者，號曰犀首，亦以談說顯名。
value.en: There was also Gongsun Yan of Wei, called Rhino’s Head, who won fame by talk alone.
value.literal: There was also Gongsun Yan of Wei, styled Rhino’s Head, who likewise won fame by persuasion.

value.zh: 其餘蘇代、蘇厲、周最、樓緩之徒，紛紜遍於天下，務以辯詐相高，不可勝紀。
value.en: Su Dai, Su Li, Zhou Zui, Lou Huan, and the rest swarmed the world, each trying to outtalk the other—too many to count.
value.literal: The rest—Su Dai, Su Li, Zhou Zui, Lou Huan, and the like—swarmed across the world, striving to outdo one another in sophistry and deceit, beyond numbering.

value.zh: 而儀、秦、衍最著。
value.en: Yet Yi, Qin, and Yan stood foremost.
value.literal: Yet Yi, Qin, and Yan were the most renowned.

value.zh: 《孟子》論之曰：或謂：「張儀、公孫衍，豈不大丈夫哉！
value.en: Mencius wrote: Some say, “Zhang Yi and Gongsun Yan—were they not true men!
value.literal: Mencius discussed them, saying: Some say, “Zhang Yi and Gongsun Yan—were they not great men!

value.zh: 一怒而諸侯懼，安居而天下熄。」
value.en: One burst of wrath and the lords trembled; one year of peace and the world went still.”
value.literal: In anger the feudal lords feared; at rest the world was stilled.”

value.zh: 孟子曰：「是惡足以為大丈夫哉？
value.en: Mencius said, “How could such men be called true men?
value.literal: Mencius said, “How can such men suffice to be great men?

value.zh: 君子立天下之正位，行天下之正道，得志則與民由之，不得志則獨行其道，富貴不能淫，貧賤不能移，威武不能詘，是之謂大丈夫。」
value.en: A gentleman stands in the right place and walks the right path. When his will is done he shares it with the people; when it is not he walks alone. Wealth cannot seduce him, poverty cannot move him, power cannot bend him—that is a true man.”
value.literal: The gentleman stands in the world’s right place, walks the world’s right path; when his will is fulfilled he shares it with the people, when it is not he walks his path alone—wealth and honor cannot dissolve him, poverty and low estate cannot shift him, force and might cannot bend him: this is called a great man."

value.zh: 揚子《法言》曰：或問：「儀、秦學乎鬼谷術而習乎縱橫言，安中國者各十餘年，是夫？」
value.en: Master Yang’s Fayan says: Someone asked, “Zhang Yi and Su Qin studied under Guiguzi and mastered coalition rhetoric; each held the Central States at peace for more than ten years—is that true?”
value.literal: Master Yang’s Fayan says: Someone asked, “Zhang Yi and Su Qin studied the arts of Guiguzi and practiced coalition rhetoric; each kept the Central States secure for more than ten years—is that so?”

value.zh: 曰：「詐人也。
value.en: He answered, “Frauds.
value.literal: He replied, “They were deceivers.

value.zh: 聖人惡諸。」
value.en: The sages despised men like that.”
value.literal: The sages abhorred such men.”

value.zh: 曰：「孔子讀而儀、秦行，何如也？」
value.en: He said, “Suppose Confucius read the classics while Zhang Yi and Su Qin carried on as they did—what then?”
value.literal: He said, “If Confucius read [the classics] but Zhang Yi and Su Qin acted [as they did]—what of that?”

value.zh: 曰：「甚矣鳳鳴而鷙翰也！」
value.en: He replied, “As absurd as a phoenix singing while a hawk strikes!”
value.literal: He replied, “How far apart are the phoenix’s cry and the hawk’s strike!”

value.zh: 「然則子貢不為歟？」
value.en: “Then did not Zi Gong do likewise?”
value.literal: “Then would Zi Gong not have done the same?”

value.zh: 曰：「亂而不解，子貢恥諸。
value.en: He said, “To stir disorder and not set it right—Zi Gong would be ashamed.
value.literal: He said, “To create disorder and not resolve it—Zi Gong would be ashamed of that.

value.zh: 說而不富貴，儀、秦恥諸。」
value.en: To persuade without winning wealth and rank—Zhang Yi and Su Qin would be ashamed.”
value.literal: To persuade without wealth and rank—Zhang Yi and Su Qin would be ashamed of that.”

value.zh: 或曰：「儀、秦其才矣乎，跡不蹈已？」
value.en: Someone asked, “Were Zhang Yi and Su Qin truly talented—walking where no one had walked?”
value.literal: Someone asked, “Were Zhang Yi and Su Qin men of talent, treading paths none had walked before?”

value.zh: 曰：「昔在任人，帝而難之，不以才矣。
value.en: He said, “Long ago there was a man of ability; the Emperor found him hard to use and did not keep him for talent alone.
value.literal: He said, “In antiquity there was a man of ability; the Emperor found him difficult and did not employ him for talent alone.

value.zh: 才乎才，非吾徒之才也。」
value.en: Talent? Talent—that is not the talent of our kind.”
value.literal: Talent? Talent—that is not the talent of our fellowship.”

value.zh: 資治通鑑 第064卷
value.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 64
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 64

value.zh: 尚兵既至，諸將皆以為：「此歸師，人自為戰，不如避之。」
value.en: When Shang's army arrived, his commanders argued: "These are men hurrying home to save their city. They will fight as if each man alone mattered. We ought to avoid them."
value.literal: When Shang's army had arrived, the generals all considered: "This is a returning army; each man will fight for himself — better to avoid it."

value.zh: 操曰：「尚從大道來，當避之；
value.en: Cao Cao said, "If Shang comes by the main road, we should avoid him;
value.literal: Cao Cao said: "If Shang comes by the great road, we ought to avoid him;

value.zh: 配厲聲曰：「汝為降虜，審配為忠臣。
value.en: Shen Pei shouted back, "You are a turncoat. I am a loyal minister.
value.literal: Pei said in a harsh voice: "You are a surrendered captive; Shen Pei is a loyal minister.

value.zh: 雖死，豈羨汝生邪！」
value.en: Even in death, why should I envy your life?"
value.literal: Though I die, why should I envy your living?"

value.zh: 臨行刑，叱持兵者令北向，曰：「我君在北也。」
value.en: At the moment of execution he ordered the executioners to turn him north, saying, "My lord is in the north."
value.literal: Facing execution, he shouted at those holding the weapons to make him face north, saying: "My lord is in the north."

value.zh: 若循西山來者，此成禽耳。」
value.en: but if he comes by the western hills, he will be easy prey."
value.literal: If he comes along the western hills, this will be catching prey."

value.zh: 尚果循西山來，東至陽平亭，去鄴十七里，臨滏水為營。
value.en: Shang did come by the western hills, reached Yangping Pavilion seventeen li from Ye, and made camp on the Fu River.
value.literal: Shang indeed came along the western hills, proceeding east to Yangping Pavilion, seventeen li from Ye, and encamped on the Fu River.

value.zh: 夜，舉火以示城中，城中亦舉火相應。
value.en: At night he lit signal fires for the city, and the city answered with fires of its own.
value.literal: At night he raised fires to signal the city; the city also raised fires in answer.

value.zh: 配出兵城北，欲與尚對決圍。
value.en: Shen Pei led troops out from the north gate, intending to link up with Shang and break the siege.
value.literal: Pei led troops out from the north of the city, wishing to meet Shang and break the encirclement face to face.

value.zh: 操逆擊之，敗還，尚亦破走，依曲漳為營，操遂圍之。
value.en: Cao Cao counterattacked and drove Shen Pei back. Shang was also routed and withdrew to the Qu Zhang to make camp, where Cao Cao besieged him.
value.literal: Cao Cao struck them in reverse, defeated them and they retreated; Shang was also routed and fled, relying on the Qu Zhang for an encampment — Cao Cao then encircled him.

value.zh: 未合，尚懼，遣使求降；
value.en: Before the ring closed, Shang, alarmed, sent envoys to sue for peace;
value.literal: Before the encirclement closed, Shang was afraid and sent envoys to beg surrender;

value.zh: 操不聽，圍之益急。
value.en: Cao Cao refused and tightened the siege.
value.literal: Cao Cao would not listen and pressed the encirclement the more urgently.

value.zh: 尚夜遁，保祁山，操復進圍之。
value.en: Shang fled by night to Qishan. Cao Cao pursued and besieged him again.
value.literal: Shang fled by night, took refuge at Qishan — Cao Cao again advanced and encircled him.

value.zh: 尚將馬延、張顗等臨陳降，眾大潰，尚奔中山。
value.en: Shang's generals Ma Yan and Zhang Yi surrendered on the field. His army collapsed, and Shang fled to Zhongshan.
value.literal: Shang's generals Ma Yan, Zhang Yi, and others surrendered before the battle line; the masses greatly collapsed, and Shang fled to Zhongshan.

value.zh: 盡收其輜重，得尚印綬、節鉞及衣物，以示城中，城中崩沮。
value.en: Cao Cao captured all his supplies, along with Shang's seals, credentials, and regalia, and displayed them before Ye. The city's morale shattered.
value.literal: [Cao Cao] took all his baggage train, obtained Shang's seal ribbon, tally and axe of authority, and clothing, and displayed them to the city — within the city spirits collapsed in dismay.
